title: Footprint: cell aggregation, imbalance detection and cell rendering
body:
## Context
**E18 Footprint** is the first and heaviest epic of the R2 "Order-flow beta" train (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 6, sprints S10-S11, 55 engineering points (see the sizing note below), area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** `orderflow`, story domain **FP**). The roadmap scope line reads verbatim: *"Backend cell aggregation (M9): bid x ask volume per price per bar, delta, cumulative delta, and imbalance detection with configurable ratio and diagonal/horizontal modes; display modes (bid x ask, delta, volume, profile-in-bar); tick-size aggregation with automatic grouping; value-area and POC per bar; text LOD (hide glyphs below a per-cell pixel-width threshold); imbalance encoded by colour and outline pattern so colour is never the only carrier; cell hover/keyboard inspection"*.

Two roadmap statements make this epic structurally special:
- section 11.3 risk table: *"E18 footprint - the heaviest render path; sets the ceiling for the rest of R2. Scheduled first in R2, with the text-LOD strategy already proven in E06."*
- section 11.2 critical path: `E02 -> E06 -> E11 -> E12 -> E18 -> E26 -> E38 -> E44 -> E46 -> GA`. E18 is on the critical path; E19 (profiles), E20 (Deep-Stats), E23 (CVD) and E26 (replay) all sit behind it in the dependency graph (section 11.1: `E18 --> E19`, `E18 --> E20`, `E18 --> E23`, `E18 --> E26`).

Every number this epic renders is computed **locally** - `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 4 opens with *"All of this is computed locally from `TradeEvent`; Bybit publishes nothing footprint-shaped."* Bybit gives the taker side directly on `publicTrade`, so aggressor reconstruction is unnecessary: `if trade.side == "buy": ask_volume += qty else: bid_volume += qty`. The algorithms (diagonal imbalance with the zero-denominator rule, stacked runs, unfinished auction, per-bar POC and value area with its documented tie-break order) are fully specified in that section and must be implemented exactly, not re-derived.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (all 10 FP stories):** US-FP-001 (Must), US-FP-002 (Must), US-FP-003 (Must/Should), US-FP-004 (Must), US-FP-005 (Must/Should), US-FP-006 (Must/Should), US-FP-007 (Must), US-FP-008 (Must), US-FP-009 (Must/Should), US-FP-010 (Must).

- **Backend (M9 `orderflow`)**: `FootprintEngine` (`on_trade`, `on_bar_update`, `recompute_flags`) producing `BarFootprint`/`FootprintCell`/`ImbalanceFlag` per `24-internal-schemas.md` section 4.1; `FootprintConfig` (section 4.7) as the single configuration contract.
- **Persistence**: QuestDB `footprint_cells` (`21-database-schema.md` section 4.9) with `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol, bar_family, bar_param, price)`; Parquet cold tier `cold/footprint_cells/symbol=.../bar_family=.../bar_param=.../dt=...`; retention 30 d hot / 12 mo cold, rebuildable from `trades`.
- **API**: `GET /api/v1/market/footprint` and `POST /api/v1/market/footprint/recompute` (`22-api-openapi.yaml`), schemas `FootprintCell`, `FootprintImbalance`, `FootprintBar`, `FootprintResponse`.
- **WS**: topic `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with options `price_grouping`, `imbalance_ratio`, `min_stack`, `min_imbalance_volume`, `history` (<=200); binary `body_kind` 5 (33-byte cells with flag bits 0 buy-imbalance, 1 sell-imbalance, 2 in-stack, 3 POC); coalescing rule "per (bar, price) cell, values summed for the same bar, replaced across bars" (`23-ws-protocol.md` sections 3.4, 6.1, 8.2, 14.4).
- **Chart engine**: `FootprintSeries` (CMP-182) over `FootprintCell` (CMP-109) consuming the prefix-sum `FootprintData` layout (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 8); all four `cellType` values and both `displayMode` values; SDF glyph text with the LOD ladder and hysteresis; imbalance markers; POC/VA/unfinished-auction markers via CMP-195.
- **Screens**: SCR-030 (chart panel hosting footprint), SCR-032 (footprint settings dialog), SCR-042 (`Alt+F` profile/box toggle entry point, footprint on/off via CMP-222), SCR-045 (data-table alternative parity for cells), SCR-056 (imbalance tracker panel, the E18-owned half: US-FP-007/US-FP-008 rows).
- **Components**: CMP-109 FootprintCell, CMP-182 FootprintSeries, CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator, CMP-195 AnnotationMarker, CMP-197 ChartTooltip, CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle (footprint `aria-pressed` toggle), CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-228 PreviewTile, CMP-046 Drawer (cell detail), CMP-049 Table, CMP-011 Tag/Chip.
- **ADR**: ADR-0016 footprint aggregation, display-time recompute and text-LOD strategy.

## Out of scope
- Session / visible-range / fixed-range / composite **profiles** and TPO - E19 (this epic ships only the per-bar mini profile of `24-internal-schemas.md` section 4.5).
- Deep-Stats strip rows and CSV export - E20.
- Imbalance **tracker analytics** beyond rendering E18's own diagonal/stacked flags (detector inspector, absorption scoring, z-scores) - E25 owns SCR-056's US-DET-004 half.
- CVD and cumulative-delta panes - E23 (E18 emits per-bar `delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta` only).
- Replay-driven footprint playback - E26 (E18 guarantees a single pipeline so replay reuses it; it does not build the replay clock).
- Order-based ("per-order arrival") footprint input - impossible on Bybit (no L3/MBO); the control is **absent** from the UI with an explanatory note (US-FP-005 scenario 3).
- Android, any separate admin app, non-Bybit venues, non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Footprint renders end to end from live data
  Given the recorder holds >= 1 trading day of BTCUSDT trades
  And a 5m footprint pane is open on SCR-030
  When live trades arrive over trades.BTCUSDT
  Then per-price bid and ask volumes, per-bar delta, POC, value area, diagonal and stacked imbalance flags render within 250 ms of the coalesced footprint frame
  And the same values are returned by GET /api/v1/market/footprint for the same window

Scenario: Values match an independent offline recomputation
  Given a full recorded symbol-day golden fixture
  When the footprint is recomputed offline in DuckDB over the Parquet tier
  Then every cell, imbalance flag, POC, value-area boundary and unfinished-auction flag matches the served values within floating-point tolerance
  And any drift fails CI

Scenario: Frame budget holds at the documented density
  Given 60 visible bars x 40 price levels with cell numerals shown
  When the viewport is panned and zoomed for 5 minutes
  Then p95 frame time is <= 16.6 ms and the frame rate never falls below 30 fps
  And when the cell budget is exceeded the view collapses to the compact profile representation with a "zoom in for numbers" hint instead of dropping frames

Scenario: Colour is never the only carrier
  Given a colour-vision-deficiency simulation and a greyscale render
  Then imbalance is still distinguishable by outline pattern, delta by sign and directional glyph, and POC/value area by border and text label

Scenario: Display-time parameters never refetch
  Given a loaded footprint range
  When the imbalance ratio, minimum stack, value-area percentage or price grouping is changed
  Then flags and buckets are recomputed from cached native-tick cells with no trade re-read and no history refetch

Scenario: Partial history is explicit
  Given the recorder started at 2027-01-15T00:00:00Z for this symbol
  When a window beginning before that timestamp is requested
  Then the pane shows the partial-history state naming that first available timestamp and does not render silently truncated bars
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Authoritative model**: backend owns `FootprintConfig`; `FootprintOptions` in the engine (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 8) mirrors it field-for-field where they overlap.
- **Storage-time vs display-time split** (the load-bearing decision of this epic): cells accumulate and persist at **native tick resolution**; `aggregation_ticks`, `imbalance_ratio`, `min_stack`, `value_area_pct`, `zero_policy` and the noise filter are **display-time** parameters resolved by `recompute_flags` over cached cells. Only an input-source change triggers `POST /market/footprint/recompute`.
- **Grid keys are integers**: `price_ticks = round((price - price_origin) / tick_size)` (`24-internal-schemas.md` C5). Floats as grid keys manufacture phantom levels. A `metadata_version` bump (tick-size change) invalidates cached aggregates and schedules a rebuild (section 13.6).
- **Transport**: prefix-sum typed arrays (`barIndexOffsets`, `cellPriceLevel`, `cellBidVol`, `cellAskVol`, `cellTradeCount`), transferable to the engine worker with zero copies.
- **Cadence**: forming-bar footprint coalesced to at most 100 ms server-side; the closing update is always sent immediately; WS default throttle for the topic is 250 ms.
- **Memory**: `BarFootprint` evicted beyond the 2 000 most recent bars per (symbol, spec) and re-materialised from QuestDB/Parquet on scroll-back.

## Test plan
- Unit: aggregation, bucketing, diagonal ratio with all three `zero_policy` values, edge levels, stacked runs with and without gaps, unfinished/finished auction, POC tie-break ladder, both value-area algorithms. >= 85% line coverage on the backend and engine packages.
- Contract: OpenAPI and WS JSON-Schema validation of `FootprintResponse` and `FootprintUpdate`; binary `body_kind` 5 round-trip.
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures - normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.
- Golden fixture: one recorded symbol-day, version-controlled expected outputs, DuckDB cross-check.
- E2E (Playwright, web + Electron): toggle footprint, switch all cell and display modes, change thresholds, keyboard-navigate cells, open the settings dialog, verify the table alternative.
- Perf: dedicated CI footprint benchmark per R2 quality gates; engine benchmark B3-class scene.
- A11y: axe-core on the DOM-mirror layer, manual screen-reader pass, greyscale and CVD simulation.

## Security notes
Data classification: market data (non-secret) plus user configuration. Threats per `04-security-program.md`: (a) **DoS by unbounded window** - `bars x price_levels <= 200 000 cells` enforced with `400 validation_failed / footprint_window_too_large`, plus `history <= 200` on the WS topic; (b) **resource exhaustion via recompute** - `POST /market/footprint/recompute` requires `recording:write`, an idempotency key and a job queue with concurrency limits; (c) **RBAC** - `GET /market/footprint` requires `marketdata:read`; (d) **injection** - `symbol`, `bar_type`, `param` are validated against the closed instrument and bar-spec vocabularies before reaching QuestDB. Every state-changing action (settings save, recompute request) writes an audit record with `chart.footprint_settings_changed`.

## Accessibility notes
Every visible cell is mirrored by an off-screen DOM node (`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.1 canvas control surrogate): focusable, `aria-label` composing "Price 65,430; bid 12.4; ask 8.1; delta +4.3", arrow keys moving cell-to-cell across price and time, `Enter` opening the cell-detail Drawer (CMP-046). The mirror always carries the full value **regardless of zoom-driven text hiding**. SCR-045 provides equal-status table access (`Alt+T`). Imbalance uses colour **and** outline pattern; delta uses colour **and** sign/glyph; POC/VA use border/pattern plus text. A CVD-safe palette variant ships in the design tokens.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #1 frame time <= 16.6 ms p95 (hard), #2 never below 30 fps (hard), #3 WS tick -> screen p95 < 100 ms (hard, R2 exit gate). Engine target from `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 2: *2 500 visible cells with 2 numbers each at 60 fps with graceful LOD below cell-text legibility*; glyph budget ~12 500 glyphs in one instanced draw call, CI asserts <= 2.0 ms total. US-FP-001 NFR: >= 55 fps at 60 bars x 40 levels with numerals.

## Observability
Metrics: `footprint_cells_per_bar` (histogram), `footprint_recompute_duration_seconds`, `footprint_engine_lag_ms`, `footprint_ws_coalesced_total`, `footprint_eviction_total`, `footprint_rebuild_jobs_total{status}`. Logs: structured on recompute start/finish with symbol, window, cell count. Traces: span from ingestion receipt through `FootprintEngine.on_trade` to WS emit, correlated with the frontend paint span per budget #3. Audit: `chart.footprint_settings_changed`, `market.footprint_recompute_requested`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with disposition recorded here.
- [ ] All 10 FP user stories demonstrated end-to-end on staging (demo) at a Sprint Review with Owner acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Golden-fixture parity green in CI; footprint benchmark green; zero open P0/P1 against E18 scope.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85% backend/engine, >= 80% frontend on touched packages.
- [ ] `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `21-database-schema.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md` reflect shipped behaviour.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-030/SCR-032/SCR-045/SCR-056; manual screen-reader pass recorded; keyboard cell navigation verified.
- [ ] perf: budgets #1/#2/#3 recorded against the full-density scene.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] design: CDO/designer sign-off on SCR-030, SCR-032, SCR-056 checklists; design-QA sweep closed.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression and exploratory pass recorded.

## Dependencies
- **E12 Bar builders & series rendering** - footprint is keyed to bar boundaries produced by the bar builders; `E12 --> E18` in the roadmap graph.
- **E16 Recorder, retention & disk budget** - history depth and the rebuild source; `E16 --> E18`.
- **E11 Chart engine core** - pane, price axis, viewport, LOD scheduler and SDF text pipeline.
- **E17 WS protocol** - envelope, sequencing, binary framing and coalescing machinery the `footprint.*` topic plugs into.
- **E06 Chart-engine spike & ADR** - the text-LOD strategy this epic assumes is already proven; the SCR-030/SCR-032 design sign-off gate references its evidence.

title: UX research: how order-flow traders read and act on footprint cells
body:
## Context
E18 introduces the densest information surface in the product: a grid of per-bar, per-price cells each carrying up to two numbers, a colour, an outline and optional markers. Before any pixel is drawn we need evidence for four decisions that cannot be recovered later without re-drawing everything: (1) which cell mode traders actually read at which zoom, (2) at what cell height numerals stop being useful (feeding E18-K01's measured LOD threshold), (3) whether imbalance is read as a per-cell marker or as a zone bracket, and (4) what a trader wants to do the moment they notice a cell ("focus imbalance", "copy cell stats", "replay from here" are the three context-menu items SCR-030 currently assumes).

The personas are `docs/plan/10-personas.md` P1 (owner/discretionary order-flow trader) and M1 (account manager). This is a **new interaction** - nothing in R0/R1 has a canvas grid with per-cell focus - so `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 requires research before wireframes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-6 moderated sessions with the Owner and any available order-flow traders, using DeepCharts/Sierra/ATAS-style reference screenshots plus a clickable static prototype of SCR-030 at three zoom levels.
- Findings memo in `docs/research/digests/` covering: preferred default cell mode (bid x ask vs delta), read order within a cell, minimum comfortable cell height in px, imbalance representation preference (per-cell marker vs zone bracket vs both), context-menu action ranking, and the acceptability of the compact-profile collapse at high density.
- A prioritised decision list feeding E18-D02 wireframes and E18-K01's threshold-measurement plan.
- Validation that US-FP-005's "order-based input is absent, not disabled" framing reads as honest rather than as a missing feature.

## Out of scope
Visual design, tokens, motion, any Figma artboard, DOM-ladder or profile research (E21/E19 own theirs).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Evidence for the default cell mode
  Given at least 4 completed sessions
  When findings are synthesised
  Then the memo states the default cell mode with the count of participants preferring it and the reasons given

Scenario: Legibility floor is evidenced, not guessed
  When participants view the prototype at 4 px, 6 px, 8 px and 12 px cell heights
  Then the memo records the height at which each participant stops reading numerals
  And that figure is handed to E18-K01 as the starting point for the measured textLod threshold

Scenario: Contradictory findings are surfaced, not averaged
  Given participants disagree on imbalance representation
  Then the memo records both positions with rationale and proposes a per-user setting or a default plus override, rather than reporting a mean
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype uses static rendered PNGs of real recorded BTCUSDT 5m data (no engine dependency, so this can run in S08 before E18-S01 exists). Sessions recorded with consent; recordings stored in the research drive, not in the repo. Use the `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md` journey-map format for the synthesis.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validation is peer review of the memo by the CDO and the chart-engine lead.

## Security notes
Session recordings may contain participant faces and voices - PII. Store in the access-controlled research drive, redact names in the published memo, delete raw recordings after synthesis per the research data policy. No product data classification impact.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session run with a participant using a screen reader or at 200% zoom, to sanity-check that the DOM-mirror and SCR-045 table-alternative plan is credible before it is designed.

## Performance notes
N/A - but the legibility-floor finding is a direct input to performance budget #1, since cell text is the dominant glyph cost.

## Observability

WCAG 2.2 AA: >= 4.5:1 for all cell text and labels, >= 3:1 for meaningful non-text boundaries (cell borders carrying POC/VA meaning), >= 24x24 px targets for every interactive control in SCR-032 and SCR-056, visible focus ring specified for the focused cell in the DOM mirror (the ring is drawn on the canvas, synchronised with the mirror focus). ## Performance notes
Constrain the design to the measured glyph budget: 2 500 visible cells x 2 numbers in one instanced draw call, <= 2.0 ms total (CI-asserted). Any design element requiring a second text pass or a per-cell texture must be justified against that budget with the chart-engine lead's agreement.

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the footprint surfaces
body:
## Context
Footprint has more moving parts than any prior surface: the forming bar's cells change up to 10 times a second, imbalance flags appear and disappear as thresholds are met, the LOD ladder switches text on and off while zooming, and stacked-imbalance zones transition virgin -> crossed. Timebox: **4 days**, agreed with the Architect. This spike is **not** expected to produce production-shippable code; the harness may be promoted, the rendering experiments are throwaway.

## Scope / Deliverables
Questions to answer, with recorded numbers on the reference machine (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 3.1) in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2:
1. At what per-cell pixel height do numerals stop being legible in the shipped design-system mono face at each density class? (Cross-check against E18-D01's user-reported floor.) -> sets `lodTextThresholdPx`.
2. What is the measured cost of the target scene: 2 500 visible cells x 2 numbers (~12 500 glyphs) in one instanced draw - CPU batching and GPU time? Target <= 2.0 ms total.
3. Where is the cell-count ceiling at which the compact-profile collapse must engage (US-FP-001 "density limit" scenario)?
4. Does per-cell glyph-run caching (pre-formatted strings + atlas offsets, invalidated on format change) hold at a 10 Hz forming-bar update rate, or does re-formatting dominate?
5. What is the incremental cost of imbalance outlines and POC/VA/unfinished markers on top of the base cell grid?
6. Does the prefix-sum `FootprintData` layout (`barIndexOffsets` / `cellPriceLevel` / `cellBidVol` / `cellAskVol` / `cellTradeCount`) transfer to the worker without a copy, and what is the transfer cost for a 200-bar prepend during scroll-back?

  When the spike completes

  And it is handed to E18-D05 for the design sign-off gate

Scenario: Glyph budget verdict
  Given the 12 500-glyph scene
  When total frame cost is measured
  Then if it is <= 2.0 ms the instanced-SDF path is confirmed for E18-S01
  And if it exceeds 2.0 ms the spike reports which of (a) fewer size classes, (b) abbreviated number formatting by default, (c) a lower default cell budget is the chosen mitigation, and that choice is recorded in ADR-0016

Scenario: Runtime parity
  Given the same scene in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2
  Then any runtime whose frame time differs by more than 25% from the best is named in the report with the suspected cause

## Context

## Scope / Deliverables
- **E2E specs** (Playwright, run against web and the Electron shell):
  - Toggle footprint with `F`; verify the pane renders and the legend states the bucket size.
  - Cycle all four cell modes and both display modes; assert no `/market/footprint` request is issued (proving the cached-aggregate contract).
  - Change the imbalance ratio and stack depth; assert flag and zone counts change as the golden fixture predicts, with no refetch.
  - Change the input source; assert a recompute job starts, progress is shown and the pane updates on completion; assert failure renders an actionable message with the code in a details disclosure.
  - Per-symbol defaults: save for BTCUSDT, open ETHUSDT, assert independence; reload the workspace and assert persistence.
  - Two panes on one symbol with different display modes; save/reload the workspace.
  - Keyboard-only traversal of a bar's cells and `Alt+T` parity against the canvas values.
  - Partial-history state naming the first available timestamp on a recorder-gap fixture.
  - Absence of the order-based input option in the DOM, and absence of an `(estimated)` badge on exact sources.
  - Density collapse: zoom past the cell budget, assert the compact representation and the "zoom in for numbers" hint.
- **Integration specs** against the R2-mandated recorded fixtures: normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol. Each asserts continuity (no duplicate or missing bar at the REST→WS seam) and correct gap declaration.

title: Footprint performance benchmark, load profile and CI gate
body:
## Context
The R2 quality-gate table states: *"Perf — Budgets #1, #2, #3, #14 all hard gates; heatmap and footprint each have a dedicated benchmark in CI."* This ticket builds footprint's half of that gate by promoting the E18-K01 harness into a maintained CI benchmark and adding the WS load profile that proves budget #3 for the footprint topic.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** in CI (adopted from E18-K01's harness): the target scene — 60 visible bars × 40 price levels with numerals (US-FP-001 NFR), plus the heavier 2 500-cell / ~12 500-glyph scene from `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 2. Asserts p95 frame time ≤ 16.6 ms, p99 ≤ 22 ms, glyph batching ≤ 2.0 ms, and ≥ 55 fps on the US-FP-001 scene. Runs headless Chromium on PRs, Electron nightly.
- **Worst-case / degradation benchmark**: footprint + all overlays in a multi-pane layout, asserting the 30 fps floor (budget #2) is never breached and that the degradation strategy engages visibly (the non-colour-only "reduced detail" indicator) rather than silently dropping frames.
- **Mode matrix**: benchmark each cell mode and display mode separately, so a regression can be attributed (bid×ask is the glyph-heaviest; profile must be measurably cheapest).
- **WS load profile (k6)**: 20 concurrent pane subscriptions across 10 symbols on the `footprint.*` topic against staging with recorded fixtures, asserting budget #3 (tick → screen p95 < 100 ms, p99 < 250 ms) and budget #6 (backend-internal ≤ 20 ms p95), plus the ADR-0005 criteria (≥ 40% bandwidth and ≥ 30% decode-time reduction for binary vs JSON on this topic).
- **Backend engine benchmark**: `FootprintEngine` per-trade cost and `recompute_flags` over 200 bars × 40 cells (target ≤ 30 ms), plus the 24 h / 10-symbol ingestion soak assertion that footprint work does not break budget #5 (zero undetected loss) or #8 (memory per symbol).
- **Memory soak**: the 2-hour Playwright chart-engine soak with a footprint pane open, asserting no monotonic growth (budget #7) and a bounded DOM-mirror node count.
- Threshold provenance: CI thresholds are set from ADR-0016's recorded numbers; the benchmark fails the build on regression beyond the agreed band and publishes a trend.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E18-Q02), the a11y audit (E18-Q04), heatmap benchmarks (E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budgets asserted, not merely measured
  When the benchmark runs
  Then it fails the build if p95 frame time exceeds 16.6 ms on the target scene
  And it fails if the worst-case scene drops below 30 fps at any sampled point

Scenario: Regression attribution
  Given a deliberate 20 percent slowdown introduced in glyph batching
  Then the benchmark fails and the stage-attribution report names the text stage, not just the total

Scenario: WS budget under realistic load
  Given 20 concurrent footprint subscriptions across 10 symbols for 30 minutes
  Then tick to screen p95 is under 100 ms and p99 under 250 ms
  And the backend-internal sub-span is asserted at or under 20 ms p95 independently

Scenario: Binary encoding earns its place
  Then the footprint topic shows at least 40 percent bandwidth and 30 percent decode-time reduction versus JSON
  And if it does not, the result is reported as an ADR-0005 finding rather than quietly accepted

Scenario: No leaks
  Given a two hour soak with a footprint pane open
  Then process memory shows no monotonic growth beyond the documented variance band
  And the DOM-mirror node count stays proportional to visible cells
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reference hardware per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 3.1; results are only comparable on it, so CI pins the runner class and records it in the report.
- Measure with `Performance.mark()/measure()` at the section 4.3 stage boundaries and export structured spans, matching E18-K01's format so spike and CI numbers are directly comparable.
- Use SwiftShader only for golden images, never for timing.
- The k6 profile drives staging with recorded fixtures, per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 8's rule against load-testing live Bybit.

## Test plan
Self-verification by seeded regressions (glyph slowdown, extra draw call in the pattern pass, an unbounded mirror rebuild). Each must fail the gate and be attributed correctly.

## Security notes
Load testing runs against staging only, never live. The k6 profile uses dedicated test credentials from the CI secret store and respects the demo environment's constraints. Confirm the load profile cannot be pointed at a live endpoint by configuration accident — fail closed on an unexpected host.

## Accessibility notes
The worst-case benchmark explicitly asserts that the degradation indicator is not colour-only and that the DOM mirror stays synchronised with what is rendered — `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 4.4 lists mirror desync as never acceptable, including under degradation.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance gate. Budgets in scope: #1, #2, #3, #5, #6, #7, #8. Record every figure on the ticket and in ADR-0016's consequences if it differs from the spike.

## Observability
Benchmark trend published per commit; alert on a sustained regression trend even when still inside the band, so slow rot is visible before it breaks the gate.

## Context
R2 exit criterion 10 requires an a11y pass on every new view *"incl. keyboard-navigable footprint cells"*, and the R2 a11y quality gate adds that colour-blind-safe palettes must be verified for the green/red conventions. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 makes WCAG 2.2 AA default-on with no "internal tool" exception. This is the independent audit that E18-S11's implementation must survive.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated**: axe-core runs on SCR-030 (with the DOM-mirror layer), SCR-032, SCR-045 and SCR-056, in dark, light and high-contrast themes, at 100%, 125% and 200% zoom, wired as CI checks.
- **Manual screen-reader passes**: NVDA (Windows/Chromium and Electron) and VoiceOver (macOS/Safari where applicable), covering cell navigation, the settings dialog, the imbalance tracker and the table alternative. Recorded as evidence with notes per `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- **Keyboard-only pass**: every function reachable and operable without a mouse, including mode switching, threshold changes, cell inspection, zone inspection and the data-table alternative; no keyboard traps; `Esc` behaviour consistent; focus never lost after a dialog or drawer closes.
- **Colour-independence verification**: greyscale and deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulation over every footprint state (cell modes, imbalance flags, stacked zones virgin/broken, POC/VA, noise-filtered cells, degraded mode), confirming the outline-pattern and glyph carriers. Explicit verification of the green=bid / red=ask convention and its CVD-safe alternative.
- **Contrast measurement** of cell numerals against the full heat range in all three themes, and of focus indicators at every LOD level.
- **Announcement-policy conformance**: assert the E18-D04 policy is implemented — silence on forming-cell updates, announcements only on focus movement, bar close and new stacked zones, polite never assertive.
- **Reduced motion**: `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured for every transition listed in the E18-D04 motion spec.
- Findings log with WCAG success-criterion references, severity, and disposition (fixed in-sprint or filed as a Bug with a priority label).

## Out of scope
Fixing the findings (they become Bugs or in-sprint fixes on the owning stories); the DOM ladder (E21); non-footprint parts of SCR-045.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Then axe-core reports zero violations on SCR-030, SCR-032, SCR-045 and SCR-056 across all three themes and all three zoom levels
  And the runs are wired as CI checks, not one-off manual executions

Scenario: A screen-reader user can read a bar
  Given a screen-reader user with no sight of the canvas
  When they navigate a bar's cells
  Then they can state the bid, ask and delta at each level, which level is the point of control, and whether any level is imbalanced

Scenario: Nothing depends on colour
  Given greyscale and three CVD simulations over every footprint state
  Then every distinction the design encodes with colour is also carried by pattern, glyph, sign or text

Scenario: Chatter is bounded in practice
  Given a live forming bar updating at full rate for two minutes
  Then the measured announcement count matches the E18-D04 policy
  And a screen-reader user reports the surface as usable, not noisy

Scenario: Findings are dispositioned
  Then every finding is either fixed and re-verified, or filed as a Bug with a priority label and linked here
  And no finding is left as an unresolved comment
```

Audit against WCAG 2.2 AA, focusing on 1.4.1 (use of colour), 1.4.3/1.4.11 (contrast), 2.1.1/2.1.2 (keyboard, no trap), 2.4.3 (focus order), 2.4.7 (focus visible), 2.4.11 (focus not obscured), 2.5.8 (target size ≥ 24×24), 4.1.2 (name/role/value) and 4.1.3 (status messages). The audit is the test. Re-verification after fixes is mandatory and recorded; a fix that is not re-verified leaves the finding open.

Screen-reader session recordings may capture the tester's environment — store with the other QA evidence, not in the repo. No product security surface.

`a11y_announcements_total{surface="footprint"}` is used as the objective measure for the chatter scenario.

body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-001 — Footprint volume cells (Must)**: *"As an order-flow trader, I want per-price traded volume inside each bar, so that I see where business was done."* This is the chassis story of E18 and, per `15-component-catalogue.md`, *"the highest-effort chassis piece"* in the whole component catalogue. Every other FP story renders through it.

Screen: **SCR-030** (chart panel, footprint layer). Components: **CMP-182 FootprintSeries** over **CMP-109 FootprintCell**, with **CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle** providing the footprint on/off `aria-pressed` toggle and **CMP-197 ChartTooltip** the crosshair readout.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/src/layers/footprint/` — the `footprint` series type registered in `SeriesOptionsMap`, consuming the transferable `FootprintData` layout: `barIndexOffsets: Uint32Array` (prefix sums), `cellPriceLevel: Int32Array` (ticks from `priceOrigin`), `cellBidVol`/`cellAskVol: Float32Array`, `cellTradeCount: Uint16Array`, plus `priceOrigin` and `tickSize`.
- `setData` / `append` / `prependHistory` / `setOptions` / `setVisible` on the series handle, with buffer transfer (no copies) into the engine worker.
- Bootstrap from `GET /api/v1/market/footprint`, live tail from `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` (binary `body_kind` 5 decoded to the typed-array layout directly), keyed to bars by bar open time since footprint and bars are separate subscriptions.
- Tick aggregation: `price_grouping` applied server-side per subscription; the legend shows the effective bucket size; auto mode targets ≤ 60 rows per bar.
- **Text LOD ladder** with the measured `lodTextThresholdPx` from E18-K01 and the ±15% hysteresis dead band: full numerals → abbreviated numbers → bid/ask bars → plain candle. Below the text threshold cells remain focusable and the DOM mirror still carries full values.
- **Cell-budget collapse** (US-FP-001 scenario 3): above the configured cell budget the view collapses to the compact profile representation with the "zoom in for numbers" hint rather than dropping frames.
- Footprint on/off toggle (`F` hotkey, CMP-222) and the cell tooltip on crosshair hover.
- Degraded-mode notice: "Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below N px cells" using the measured N.
- Partial-history state: "No recorded history before <timestamp> — footprint starts there", driven by `meta.recording_started_at` (global AC #7).

## Out of scope
Bid/ask split rendering (E18-S02), delta modes (E18-S03), profile/box display modes (E18-S04), colouring and noise filter (E18-S06), imbalance markers (E18-S07/S08), POC/VA markers (E18-S09), the settings dialog (E18-S10), DOM-mirror keyboard navigation (E18-S11 — this story ships the mirror nodes, S11 ships the navigation and announcements).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Render cells
  Given footprint is enabled on a 5m BTCUSDT chart
  Then each bar shows per-price-level volume aggregated at the configured price-bucket size
  And the legend states the bucket size

Scenario: Bucket size change does not refetch
  When I change the bucket from 1 tick to 5 ticks
  Then cells re-aggregate without refetching history
  And the legend updates to the new bucket size

Scenario: Density limit degrades gracefully
  Given the zoom level would render more than the configured cell budget
  Then cells collapse to a compact profile representation with a "zoom in for numbers" hint
  And the frame rate does not drop below 30 fps at any point during the transition

Scenario: LOD does not flicker
  Given a slow zoom sweep across the text-LOD threshold
  Then the hysteresis dead band produces at most one text show/hide transition per crossing

Scenario: Scroll-back paging
  Given the user pans left beyond the loaded range
  Then prior bars are fetched and prepended without re-uploading the full vertex buffer
  And the visible range does not jump

Scenario: Partial history is explicit
  Given the recorder started after the requested window begins
  Then the pane shows the partial-history state naming the first available timestamp
  And no bars are silently zero-filled

Scenario: Values below the text threshold are still available
  Given cell height is below the measured text threshold
  Then numerals are hidden on the canvas
  And the DOM-mirror label for each visible cell still carries the full bid, ask and delta values
```

## Technical notes / design
- Instanced draws throughout: one quad with per-instance attributes for cells, one instanced glyph batch for text (`26-chart-engine-design.md` sections 3.5, 3.7). Number formatting is pre-computed per cell on data update and cached as a glyph run — never formatted per frame; changing the format invalidates only the run cache.
- Memory (section 9 budget table): footprint glyph runs budgeted at ~9.6 MB for 20k bars × 40 cells × 12 B; the SDF atlas is 1 MB. Stay inside the 600 MB engine memory budget and the 450 MB per-chart-panel budget from SCR-030.
- The engine mirrors the backend contract: `FootprintOptions` field names match `FootprintConfig` where they overlap, and the backend is authoritative.
- Incremental updates must never re-upload the full vertex buffer (SCR-030 performance note); use sub-buffer updates keyed off `barIndexOffsets`.
- Degradation order under frame pressure (section on the scheduler): if over budget for 3 consecutive frames, step down one LOD level and log; footprint detail is shed before bars and never before trading overlays.

## Test plan
- Unit (Vitest): prefix-sum indexing, tick↔pixel mapping round-trips, LOD threshold selection with hysteresis, glyph-run cache invalidation, cell-budget collapse decision, buffer transfer without copy. ≥ 85% on the package.
- Golden image (Playwright + SwiftShader, ≤ 0.1% pixel diff): footprint at each LOD level, per theme.
- Integration: bootstrap-then-tail continuity (no duplicated or missing bar at the REST→WS seam); scroll-back prepend; resync after `resync_required`.
- E2E: toggle footprint with `F`, zoom through the LOD ladder, verify the hint and the degraded notice.
- Perf: the E18-K01 scene as a CI benchmark (adopted by E18-Q03).

## Security notes
Client-side rendering of public market data. Threat: **resource exhaustion in the client** — a malicious or buggy server frame claiming a huge `cell_count` must not cause an unbounded allocation; validate `cell_count` against the declared buffer length before decoding and drop the frame with a logged protocol error otherwise. No credentials or PII on this surface.

## Accessibility notes
Every **visible** cell is mirrored by an off-screen DOM node (`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.1 canvas control surrogate), `tabindex`-able with an `aria-label` composing "Price 65,430; bid 12.4; ask 8.1; delta +4.3". The mirror carries full values **regardless of zoom-driven text hiding** — this is a hard invariant recorded in ADR-0016. The canvas itself keeps `role="img"` with the rolling summary label. The mirror is built from visible cells only and recycled, never one node per loaded cell. Navigation and announcements land in E18-S11.

## Performance notes
Budgets #1 (≤ 16.6 ms p95), #2 (never below 30 fps), #3 (WS tick → screen p95 < 100 ms). US-FP-001 NFR: ≥ 55 fps with 60 visible bars × 40 price levels showing numerals, text rendered from a glyph atlas and not the DOM. SCR-030: ≥ 58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100k bars and footprint on; first bars painted ≤ 400 ms from cache, ≤ 1.2 s cold; memory ≤ 450 MB per chart panel.

## Observability
Frontend metrics via the frame harness: per-layer frame cost attributed to `footprint`, LOD level changes per minute, cell count rendered, glyph count per frame, collapse-state entries. Structured client log on protocol validation failure. The WS receipt→paint span closes budget #3's end-to-end trace.

title: Render bid/ask split cells with narrow-cell degradation
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-002 — Bid/ask split cells (Must)**: *"I want bid vs ask volume per price level, so that I can see aggression at each price."* This is the default cell mode per `21-database-schema.md` section 10's built-in template `Footprint Bid/Ask` (candle, time 1m, `cell=bid_ask`, `display=box`, imbalance 300%).

Terminology is fixed by `24-internal-schemas.md` section 4.1 because platforms disagree: **`bid_volume` = volume traded at the bid (aggressor sell); `ask_volume` = traded at the ask (aggressor buy)**. Bybit reports the taker side explicitly, so attribution is direct and needs no reconstruction — and that fact must be stated in the info popover.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `cellType: 'bid-ask'` rendering in CMP-182/CMP-109: bid-side and ask-side volume side by side with a clear separator and per-side labels.
- Per-side labels that do not rely on position alone: a `B`/`A` prefix or an equivalent glyph carrier, matching the design-system decision from E18-D03. In the accessible table (SCR-045) the sides always carry `B`/`A` glyphs.
- **Narrow-cell degradation** (US-FP-002 scenario 3): when the cell is too narrow for both numbers, degrade to a bar representation (two opposed bars scaled within the cell) with both values available in the tooltip (CMP-197) and in the DOM mirror.
- Info popover on the footprint legend documenting the taker-side attribution method (US-FP-002 scenario 2), reachable by keyboard.
- Contrast maintenance: numerals remain legible against the cell background heat via the SDF outline pass specified in E18-D03.

## Out of scope
Delta and delta+total modes (E18-S03), volume-only mode (E18-S01), the colour scales and noise filter (E18-S06), imbalance flags (E18-S07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Split display
  Given cellType is bid-ask
  Then each cell shows bid-side and ask-side volume side by side with a clear separator and per-side labels

Scenario: Taker-side attribution is documented
  When I open the footprint legend info popover
  Then it states that attribution uses the exchange-reported taker side
  And the popover is reachable and readable by keyboard and screen reader

Scenario: Narrow cells degrade rather than clip
  Given the cell is too narrow for both numbers
  Then it renders as opposed bars with no clipped or overlapping glyphs
  And both values remain available in the tooltip and in the DOM-mirror label

Scenario: Side is never encoded by colour alone
  Given a greyscale render
  Then bid and ask remain distinguishable by position plus the B/A carrier

Scenario: Attribution correctness
  Given a recorded window with known taker sides
  Then bid_volume equals the summed taker-sell quantity and ask_volume the summed taker-buy quantity at every level
  And this matches the golden-fixture recomputation
```

## Technical notes / design
- Both halves render from the same instanced quad draw with a per-instance side attribute; do not introduce a second draw call for the ask side.
- The narrow-cell decision uses the same measured pixel thresholds as the LOD ladder (one coherent switch, not a second independent heuristic) — express it as the next rung of the ladder from ADR-0016, not as an ad-hoc width check.
- Separator is drawn as part of the cell quad's shader, not as a separate line primitive, to avoid a per-cell line draw.


**Estimate rationale (re-baselined 55-pt train fit):** 3 → 2. The cell geometry, glyph atlas, text-LOD ladder and DOM mirror all land in E18-S01; this story adds a second intra-cell layout plus the narrow-cell bar degradation on top of primitives that already exist and are already tested.

## Test plan
- Unit: side attribution mapping; narrow-cell threshold selection; label composition.
- Golden image: bid-ask mode at wide, medium and narrow cell widths, per theme.
- E2E: switch to bid-ask mode, zoom until degradation triggers, assert the tooltip still carries both values.
- Parity: covered by E18-T06's cell-level comparison.
- axe: the info popover and the mirror labels.

## Security notes
No new surface. The info popover contains static product copy; no user input is interpolated.

## Accessibility notes
Per-side values are in the DOM-mirror `aria-label` in words ("bid 12.4; ask 8.1") at every rendering state including the degraded bar representation. The `B`/`A` carriers satisfy global AC #3's no-colour-only rule. The info popover is a focusable disclosure meeting the ≥ 24×24 px target rule.

## Performance notes
Bid-ask is the densest text mode (two numbers per cell) and therefore the mode the glyph budget is set against: 2 500 cells × 2 numbers ≈ 12 500 glyphs in one draw call, CI-asserted ≤ 2.0 ms. This story's benchmark run is the canonical one for budget #1.

## Observability
Frame-harness attribution distinguishes `footprint.cells` from `footprint.text` so the glyph cost of this mode is separately visible.

title: Add delta and delta+total cell modes sharing one aggregate store
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-003 — Delta and delta+total cell modes (Must/Should)**: delta mode is Must, delta+total is Should. *"I want delta (Must) and delta+total (Should) cell modes, so that I can read net aggression compactly."* The story's NFR is the load-bearing constraint: **all four cell modes share one aggregate store**, which is why mode switching is instant and refetch-free.

Screen: SCR-032 exposes the selector; SCR-030 renders the result. Built-in template `Footprint Delta` (candle, time 5m, `cell=delta`, `display=profile`) depends on this.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `cellType: 'delta'` — signed delta per cell with **sign and a directional glyph in addition to colour** (global AC #3; US-FP-003 scenario 1).
- `cellType: 'delta-total'` — delta over total volume in one cell, with a shared legend explaining the layout.
- Mode switching from cached aggregates: no refetch, no re-subscribe, no recompute round-trip — the cell store already holds bid and ask volume, and delta is derived.
- Legend updates to name the active mode and explain the delta+total layout.
- Mode persisted as part of the chart template (`chart_templates`, `21-database-schema.md`; `FootprintOptions.cellType`).

## Out of scope
The colour scales and thresholds that shade delta (E18-S06 owns `colorScale` and the noise filter), profile vs box display (E18-S04), the settings dialog UI (E18-S10 — this story ships the engine modes and the toggle path).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Delta mode
  Given cellType is delta
  Then each cell shows signed delta with an explicit sign and a directional glyph in addition to colour

Scenario: Delta plus total
  Given cellType is delta-total
  Then each cell shows delta over total volume in one cell
  And the legend explains the layout

Scenario: Mode switch is instant
  When I switch between volume, bid-ask, delta and delta-total
  Then the switch renders from cached aggregates with no network request
  And the transition completes within one frame budget

Scenario: Delta is derived, never separately stored
  Given a cell with bid 8 and ask 12
  Then delta renders as +4 in every mode that displays it
  And no second aggregate store exists for delta

Scenario: Sign survives greyscale
  Given a greyscale render of delta mode
  Then positive and negative cells remain distinguishable by sign and glyph
```

## Technical notes / design
- Delta = `ask_volume - bid_volume`, computed in the shader or at glyph-run build time from the existing `cellBidVol`/`cellAskVol` arrays. No additional typed array is uploaded.
- The directional glyph comes from the SDF atlas's existing character set (`+`, `-`, and the arrow/triangle shape agreed in E18-D03) — no atlas regeneration.
- `delta-total` is a two-line cell; its minimum legible height is one rung higher on the LOD ladder than single-number modes. Express that in the ladder, not as a special case.
- Mode is part of `FootprintOptions` and therefore part of the chart template, so a saved template restores it.

## Test plan
- Unit: delta derivation; glyph-run composition per mode; LOD rung selection for the two-line mode; template round-trip.

## Accessibility notes
The DOM-mirror label always carries bid, ask **and** delta with explicit sign regardless of the active visual mode — a screen-reader user must not lose information by the sighted user's mode choice. The directional glyph is decorative to assistive tech (the sign is in the label text); mark it `aria-hidden` in the mirror so it is not double-announced.

## Performance notes
`delta-total` renders two numbers per cell, so it shares the bid-ask glyph budget; confirm budget #1 holds in this mode too and record it. Mode switching must not trigger a full buffer re-upload — assert this in the benchmark.

Analytics event on mode change (`chart.footprint_settings_changed` with the changed key), no audit record required for a display-only preference beyond the existing settings event.

body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-004 — Profile and box display modes (Must)**: *"I want footprint drawn as a histogram profile or as numeric boxes, so that I can choose density over detail."* Profile mode is also the representation the cell-budget collapse in E18-S01 falls back to, so the two must be the same code path rather than two lookalikes.

Screens: SCR-030 (rendering), SCR-042 interval/bar-mode menu (the `Alt+F` profile-vs-box toggle entry point, per the SCR-030 hotkey list and the SCR-042 story list).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `displayMode: 'profile'` — each bar draws a horizontal histogram per price level scaled to **that bar's** maximum cell volume.
- `displayMode: 'box'` — each level draws a bordered numeric cell with heat shading.
- `Alt+F` hotkey and the SCR-042 menu entry to switch modes.
- **Per-pane independence** (US-FP-004 scenario 3): two panes on the same symbol may use different display modes; mode lives in the pane's panel config, not in a global setting.
- Mode is part of the chart template (US-FP-004 NFR).
- The collapse representation from E18-S01 is refactored to call this profile renderer, so there is exactly one histogram implementation.

## Out of scope
Session/visible-range/fixed-range profiles as a separate pane — that is E19 (`VolumeProfilePane`, CMP-183). This story is strictly the per-bar in-bar histogram.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Profile mode
  Given displayMode is profile
  Then each bar draws a horizontal histogram per price level scaled to that bar's maximum cell volume
  And bars with different maxima are each scaled independently

Scenario: Box mode
  Given displayMode is box
  Then each level draws a bordered numeric cell with heat shading

Scenario: Mixed layouts
  Given two panes on the same symbol in one workspace
  When one is set to profile and the other to box
  Then each renders independently and neither switch affects the other

Scenario: Template persistence
  Given a chart template saved with displayMode profile
  When the template is applied to a new pane
  Then that pane opens in profile mode

Scenario: One histogram implementation
  Given the cell budget is exceeded in box mode
  Then the collapse representation is rendered by the same profile code path
  And a visual diff against explicit profile mode at the same zoom shows no structural difference
```

## Technical notes / design
- Profile mode needs no glyphs, so it is the cheap mode by construction — it is the natural target for the LOD ladder's lower rungs and for the degradation strategy.
- Per-bar scaling means the histogram maximum is a per-bar uniform; compute it at data-update time and store it alongside `barIndexOffsets` rather than scanning per frame.

- Golden image: profile and box at two zooms, per theme; plus the collapse-vs-profile structural diff.

- Perf: profile mode measured separately — it should be strictly cheaper than box mode; if it is not, that is a defect.

## Security notes
No new surface. Panel config is persisted through the existing workspace endpoints with their existing RBAC.

## Accessibility notes
Profile mode hides numerals entirely, so the DOM mirror is the only value carrier — the same invariant as text-hidden LOD, and it must be verified here explicitly. Profile mode must be measurably cheaper than box mode at the same density; record both figures. It is the fallback the degradation strategy relies on, so its cost bounds the worst case for budget #2.

title: Support footprint input types and make the order-based source honestly absent
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-005 — Footprint input types (Must/Should)**: traded volume is Must; aggregated volume and number of trades are Should. The third scenario is the one that matters most for product integrity: *"the 'Order (per-order arrival)' input is absent from the UI, with an info note that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed."*

R2's goal 2 states this as a train-level principle: *"Be scrupulously honest about fidelity"*, and `11-user-stories.md` global AC #6 requires an `(estimated)` badge with an explanation popover on any heuristic view. SCR-032's state list includes *"order-based source selected → persistent '(estimated)' warning banner"* — this story resolves that tension by making the option **absent** rather than present-and-warned, per US-FP-005, and records the divergence from the SCR-032 sketch in the catalogue.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Input source `traded volume` (default, Must): cells count quantity.
- Input source `number of trades` (Should): cells show print counts instead of quantity, with the legend stating the unit.
- Input source `aggregated volume` (Should): prints at the same price, side and millisecond are merged before display, per the configured aggregation window (0–100 ms, configurable; changing it re-aggregates from stored prints via `FootprintConfig`/`orderflow.footprint.agg_window_ms`).
- **Order-based input absent**: not rendered, not disabled-with-tooltip — absent, accompanied by a persistent info note (CMP-069 InfoPanel) in SCR-032 stating that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed and therefore per-order arrival cannot be computed.
- CMP-227 EstimatedBadge wiring: this story ensures the badge is **not** shown for the three supported sources (they are exact, not estimated), and that the catalogue-level test asserting badge presence on estimated views does not produce a false positive here.
- Changing the input source is the **only** footprint setting that triggers `POST /api/v1/market/footprint/recompute`; the UI shows the recompute-in-progress state ("Recomputing footprint from recorded trades — 40 %") driven by `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`.

## Out of scope
The rest of the settings dialog (E18-S10); the recompute job implementation (E18-T05); detector-level `(estimated)` views (E25).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Number-of-trades input
  Given the input source is number of trades
  Then cells show print counts instead of quantity
  And the legend states the unit

Scenario: Aggregated volume
  Given an aggregation window of 50 ms
  Then prints at the same price, side and millisecond bucket are merged before display
  And changing the window to 0 ms re-aggregates from stored prints without re-reading the exchange

Scenario: Order input is absent, not broken
  When I open the footprint settings input-source control
  Then no "Order (per-order arrival)" option is present
  And an info note explains that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed
  And a user reading only that note can explain why the option does not exist

Scenario: Exact sources carry no estimated badge
  Given any of the three supported input sources
  Then no (estimated) badge is rendered on the footprint pane
  And the catalogue-level estimated-badge test does not flag this surface

Scenario: Input-source change rebuilds visibly
  When I change the input source
  Then a recompute job is started and its progress is shown
  And the pane shows the previous data until the rebuild completes, then updates
  And if the job fails, an actionable error in domain language is shown with the job id available in a details disclosure
```

## Technical notes / design
- Aggregation-window merging happens server-side in `FootprintEngine` (E18-T01) so live and replay share one implementation; the client only selects the window.
- The recompute path is asynchronous by design: `202 + job_id`, polled. The UI must not block the pane or clear existing data while it runs.
- Error handling follows global AC #5: domain-language message, raw code in a details disclosure.
- Record in `14-screens-catalogue.md` that SCR-032's "order-based source" state is **withdrawn** in favour of absence, so the two documents stop disagreeing.


**Estimate rationale (re-baselined 55-pt train fit):** 2 → 1. The recompute trigger, progress and failure surfaces are implemented by E18-T03/E18-S10; what remains here is the source-selection wiring, the honest absence of the order-based option with its note, and the catalogue-level assertion that no `(estimated)` badge appears on exact sources.

## Test plan
- Unit: legend unit strings per source; aggregation-window parameter plumbing; job-polling state machine including failure and cancellation.
- Integration: input-source change end-to-end against a recorded fixture, asserting a recompute job is created and the pane updates on completion.
- E2E: assert the order-based option is absent from the DOM (not merely hidden by CSS) and the info note is present and readable.
- Catalogue test: the estimated-badge enforcement test passes without listing this surface.

## Security notes
The recompute action requires `recording:write`; a `viewer` must see the input-source control in a permission-denied state rather than triggering a 403 on click. The job id is safe to display. Threat: **DoS by repeated rebuilds** — the UI disables the control while a job for that (symbol, spec) is in flight, and the server enforces the real limit (E18-T03).

## Accessibility notes
The info note is a focusable disclosure, not a hover-only tooltip. Recompute progress is announced politely at coarse intervals (start, 50%, completion, failure) — not on every poll. The legend unit change is announced when the source changes.

## Performance notes
No frame-budget impact; the aggregation window changes cell counts, which indirectly affects density — the cell-budget collapse from E18-S01 covers that case.

## Observability
Audit `chart.footprint_settings_changed` and `market.footprint_recompute_requested`; metric `footprint_input_source_changes_total{source}`.

title: Apply delta/imbalance colouring, the noise filter and non-colour alternatives
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-006 — Delta / imbalance colouring and noise filter (Must/Should)**: *"I want cells coloured by delta or imbalance with a noise filter, so that meaningful cells stand out."* Its NFR requires a **CVD-safe palette variant in the design tokens**, and its third scenario requires a pattern/glyph alternative so imbalance is distinguishable without colour. The roadmap states this as a hard scope item: *"imbalance encoded by colour **and** outline pattern so colour is never the only carrier."*

## Scope / Deliverables
- `colorScale: 'delta' | 'volume' | 'imbalance'` on `FootprintOptions`, driving the cell fill.
- **Threshold colouring**: configurable strong / medium / weak delta bands; a legend mapping each shade to its numeric range (US-FP-006 scenario 1). The legend is text, so the mapping is never colour-only.
- **Noise filter**: `noiseFilter` / `noise_filter_volume` — cells below the minimum volume render muted or blank per the setting, and **the filter state is shown in the legend** so a user never mistakes a filtered chart for a quiet market.
- **Non-colour encodings** (the a11y core of this story): imbalance carries an outline pattern in addition to colour; delta carries sign and a directional glyph; estimated data (none in E18, but the shared primitive) uses a hatch pattern. Verified in greyscale and under CVD simulation.
- **CVD-safe palette variant** shipped in the design tokens and selectable from SCR-032's `[CVD-safe]` control, applying to bid/ask and imbalance colours together as one coherent switch.
- Colour LUT generation in the engine (unit-tested per `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 13's unit-test list).

## Out of scope
Imbalance **detection** (E18-S07 renders the flags produced by E18-T02; this story defines how a flagged cell looks), the settings dialog controls themselves (E18-S10), theme tokens' authorship (E18-D03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Threshold colouring
  Given thresholds are set for strong, medium and weak delta
  Then cells are shaded accordingly
  And a legend maps each shade to its numeric range in text

Scenario: Noise filter is visible, not silent
  Given a minimum cell volume of 5
  Then cells below it are drawn muted or blank per the setting
  And the legend states that a noise filter is active and at what level

Scenario: Accessibility alternative
  Given a colour-vision-deficiency simulation and a greyscale render
  Then imbalance remains distinguishable by outline pattern
  And delta remains distinguishable by sign and directional glyph

Scenario: CVD-safe palette
  When the CVD-safe palette is selected
  Then bid, ask and imbalance colours all switch together
  And the choice persists with the chart template

Scenario: Contrast holds over the heat scale
  Given the most saturated cell fill in each theme
  Then cell numerals still meet 4.5:1 contrast using the outline pass

Scenario: Filtered cells remain accessible
  Given a cell hidden by the noise filter
  Then its DOM-mirror node is either removed consistently with the visual state or labelled as filtered
  And the choice is consistent across the canvas and SCR-045 so the two never disagree
```

## Technical notes / design
- The colour LUT is generated once per theme/scale and uploaded as a small texture; per-cell colour is a LUT lookup in the shader, not a per-cell CPU colour computation.
- Outline patterns are drawn in the same instanced quad pass using a per-instance pattern index sampling a small pattern atlas — not as extra geometry. Confirmed feasible with the chart-engine lead in E18-D03.
- The noise filter is a **display-time** parameter: filtered cells still exist in the aggregate store and in the DOM mirror decision; only rendering changes. Filtering must never alter the imbalance computation input — that is governed separately by `imbalance_min_volume` on the backend, and the two must not be conflated. Document the distinction in the legend copy.

## Test plan
- Unit: LUT generation; band assignment at exact threshold boundaries; noise-filter predicate; pattern-index mapping.
- Golden image: each colour scale × each theme × CVD-safe on/off; greyscale renders committed as evidence.
- Contrast: automated contrast assertion over the rendered numeral/fill pairs at the extremes of each scale.
- E2E: set a noise filter, assert the legend announces it; switch to CVD-safe and assert all three colour families change.
- axe: legend and controls.

## Security notes
No new surface.

## Accessibility notes
This story carries the epic's core a11y obligation (global AC #3, `05-accessibility-standard.md`): no colour-only meaning anywhere in the footprint. Evidence required at Done: greyscale screenshots, deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulations, and a contrast report. The legend is the text alternative for every colour mapping and must be reachable by keyboard from the pane. The noise-filter state is announced when changed.

## Performance notes
LUT lookup and pattern sampling must not add a draw call or a second pass; measure budget #1 before and after this story and record the delta. If the outline pattern costs more than 0.3 ms at the target scene, revisit with the chart-engine lead rather than shipping over budget.

`chart.footprint_settings_changed`; frame-harness attribution for the pattern pass.

title: Flag diagonal imbalances with configurable per-symbol thresholds
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-007 — Diagonal imbalance detection (Must)**: *"I want diagonal bid/ask imbalances flagged at a configurable ratio, so that absorption and initiative are visible instantly."* The story's NFR fixes the architecture: *"computed backend-side once per bar update and streamed as flags; default 300%"* — the client never recomputes imbalance, it renders flags. That is what keeps a rule, an alert and the chart agreeing on the same number.

Screens: SCR-030 (cell markers), SCR-056 (imbalance tracker rows — the US-FP-007 half). Components: CMP-195 AnnotationMarker (cell flag), CMP-011 Tag/Chip and CMP-049 Table (tracker rows).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Render buy/sell imbalance flags on cells from the WS binary flag bits (bit0 buy-imbalance, bit1 sell-imbalance) and the structured `imbalances[]` array, with **colour plus outline pattern** (never colour alone).
- Per-symbol threshold configuration: setting 200% for BTCUSDT persists for BTCUSDT and leaves other symbols unchanged; the change recomputes flags immediately for the loaded range with **no refetch** (server-side `recompute_flags` over cached cells, delivered via the subscription's option update).
- Thin-cell exclusion: cells below the minimum-volume filter produce no flag (US-FP-007 scenario 3), preventing noise from trivial volumes — the client renders exactly what the server flags and adds no local heuristic.
- SCR-056 rows for diagonal imbalances: time, direction, price, ratio (the **actual** computed ratio, e.g. "420%"), age; click → chart crosshair jumps to the cell and highlights it.
- Threshold single-source-of-truth behaviour required by SCR-056: thresholds are shared with SCR-032, and changing one prompts to sync the other.
- The cell context menu action "Focus imbalance" (SCR-030 right-click menu).

## Out of scope
Stacked runs and zones (E18-S08), the detector inspector and absorption analytics (E25's US-DET-004 half of SCR-056), alert creation from a level (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default 300 percent
  Given ask volume at price P exceeds bid volume at P minus one tick by 300 percent or more
  Then the cell is flagged with a marker
  And the flag is counted in the imbalance tracker panel

Scenario: Threshold change is per symbol and immediate
  When I set 200 percent for BTCUSDT
  Then flags recompute immediately for the loaded range with no history refetch
  And the per-symbol threshold persists across sessions
  And ETHUSDT panes keep their own threshold

Scenario: Thin cells excluded
  Given both cells in a diagonal comparison fall below the minimum-volume filter
  Then no imbalance is flagged

Scenario: Flags come from the server, never from the client
  Given the client receives cells without flags due to a protocol error
  Then no flag is rendered and a protocol error is logged
  And the client does not compute a substitute flag

Scenario: The actual ratio is shown
  Given a flagged cell whose computed ratio is 4.2
  Then the tracker row shows 420 percent, not the 300 percent threshold

Scenario: Threshold sync prompt
  Given thresholds differ between SCR-032 and SCR-056
  When one is changed
  Then the user is prompted to sync the other rather than the two silently diverging

Scenario: Non-colour encoding
  Given a greyscale render
  Then buy and sell imbalance flags remain distinguishable by outline pattern and direction glyph
```

## Technical notes / design
- Flags arrive as bit flags in the binary payload; decode into a per-cell instance attribute so marking costs nothing extra per frame.
- Threshold persistence is per (user, symbol) in user preferences, and is applied by re-resolving the subscription options — not by a client-side filter over already-flagged cells (which would be wrong, since raising the threshold cannot be derived from a lower-threshold flag set without the ratios; use the transmitted `ratio` only for display).
- Clicking a tracker row moves the crosshair via the existing chart command bus (the same mechanism SCR-056's "click → chart crosshair jumps" requires), not by a bespoke coupling.

## Test plan
- Unit: flag-bit decoding; per-symbol threshold persistence and resolution; ratio formatting; tracker row composition.
- Integration: threshold change round-trip asserting no `/market/footprint` refetch and correct new flag counts against the golden fixture.
- Golden image: flagged cells in both directions, per theme, greyscale evidence.
- E2E: set 200% on BTCUSDT, open ETHUSDT and assert its threshold unchanged; click a tracker row and assert the crosshair moved to the right bar and price.
- Parity: flag counts and ratios covered by E18-T06.

## Security notes
Thresholds are user preferences persisted through existing endpoints with existing RBAC; no new surface. Threat: **misleading output** — a client-side substitute computation would silently disagree with rules and alerts, so the "flags come from the server" scenario is a security-adjacent correctness control, not a style preference.

## Accessibility notes
Flagged cells announce their flag in the DOM-mirror label ("... buy imbalance 420 percent"). The tracker table (CMP-049) is a real table with sortable columns and keyboard row activation. Outline pattern plus a direction glyph carries the meaning without colour. Newly formed flags are **not** announced automatically (per the E18-D04 announcement policy) — only stacked zones are, in E18-S08.

## Performance notes
Flag rendering adds one instance attribute and reuses the pattern pass from E18-S06; budget #1 impact must be under 0.2 ms at the target scene. Tracker rows are virtualised if the list exceeds the visible window.

## Observability
Metric `footprint_imbalance_flags_rendered`; analytics `chart.footprint_settings_changed` on threshold change; audit not required (display preference).

title: Render stacked imbalance zones with virgin/broken tracking
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-008 — Stacked imbalance detection (Must)**: *"I want N consecutive imbalances flagged as a stack, so that I can find likely support/resistance shelves."* Its NFR makes this the epic's outward-facing contract: *"stacks published as domain events consumable by alerts and rules"* — E25 detectors, E40 alerts and the E35 rule engine all consume `stacked_imbalance_zone`, and `22-api-openapi.yaml` already contains a rule message template referencing `footprint.sell_stack_size` and `footprint.stack_price`.

Components: **CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator** (zone marker with virgin/crossed states distinguished by **pattern, not colour alone**), CMP-049 Table and CMP-134 DetectorEventCard on SCR-056.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Zone rendering: runs of `>= min_stack` (default 3) consecutive same-direction flagged levels drawn as a bracket beside the cells, with the **price range labelled**.
- **Zone persistence**: a zone persists as a level on the chart until price trades fully through it, then is marked "broken" (US-FP-008 scenario 2). CMP-132's `state: "virgin" | "crossed"` with `pattern.hatch` distinguishing them.
- Configurable depth: requiring 4 consecutive levels recomputes stacks and removes shallower ones, immediately and without refetch.
- SCR-056 stacked rows: time, direction, stack depth ("BUY stack x4"), price range, ratio, age, and the "only unfilled" (virgin-only) filter; click → crosshair jumps and highlights the cells.
- Consumption of the `stacked_imbalance_zone` domain event so the chart, the tracker and any future alert all read the same zone identity (`stack_id`).
- Zone lifecycle across bar updates without flicker: `stack_id` stability within a recompute means the UI diffs zones rather than rebuilding them.
- Broken-zone retention policy: broken zones remain visible for a configurable look-back and are visually distinct from virgin ones.

## Out of scope
Alert creation from a zone (E40 — SCR-056's "Create alert from this level" button is stubbed and disabled with an explanatory tooltip in R2), detector inspector (E25), rule-engine wiring (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default stack of 3
  Given 3 consecutive price levels are imbalanced in the same direction
  Then the stack is highlighted as a zone with its price range labelled

Scenario: Zone persistence and breaking
  Given a virgin stacked zone
  When price trades fully through its range
  Then it is marked broken and rendered with the crossed pattern
  And it remains listed in the tracker with a broken status rather than disappearing

Scenario: Configurable depth
  When I require 4 consecutive levels
  Then stacks recompute immediately and stacks of depth 3 disappear
  And no history is refetched

Scenario: Zones are events, not decorations
  Given a new stacked zone forms
  Then a stacked_imbalance_zone domain event is published carrying symbol, bar, price range, direction, stack size and the config that produced it
  And the chart zone and the tracker row share the same stack_id

Scenario: No flicker on the forming bar
  Given the forming bar's stack membership changes several times per second
  Then zone rendering updates are coalesced to at most 10 Hz
  And a zone does not appear and disappear more than once per 200 ms

Scenario: Opposite-direction runs never merge
  Given a buy run directly adjacent to a sell run
  Then two separate zones are rendered, never one combined zone

Scenario: Virgin versus broken without colour
  Given a greyscale render
  Then virgin and broken zones remain distinguishable by hatch pattern
```

## Technical notes / design
- Zone geometry is a small number of quads per zone — cheap. The cost is in lifecycle bookkeeping, not rendering: track zones by `stack_id`, diff on update, and apply the E18-D04 flicker policy (no appear/disappear more than once per 200 ms; hold values until the coalescing window closes).
- "Traded fully through" is evaluated server-side against subsequent bars' price ranges so the chart and any rule agree; the client renders the state it is told. Define the predicate precisely in the ticket's implementation PR and mirror it into `24-internal-schemas.md` if it is not already there.
- Broken-zone look-back is bounded (`ff`-configurable, default 200 bars) so zone count cannot grow without limit on a long session.

## Test plan
- Unit: zone diffing by `stack_id`; virgin→broken transition predicate; flicker-policy timer; look-back eviction; adjacency non-merge.
- Integration: a recorded window with a known shelf that is later traded through, asserting the exact bar at which it becomes broken, twice, identically (determinism).
- Golden image: virgin and broken zones, both directions, per theme, plus greyscale.
- E2E: change `min_stack` from 3 to 4 and assert zone count drops with no network fetch; enable "only unfilled" and assert broken zones are filtered from the list but remain on the chart per the designed behaviour.
- Event contract test: `stacked_imbalance_zone` payload validated against its schema.

## Security notes
The domain event is consumed by the rule engine, which can eventually act on it — so its integrity matters more than a display element's. Controls: the event is produced only server-side from server-computed flags; the client cannot inject one; the payload includes the config that produced it so a downstream consumer can audit why a rule fired. Note this in the E18-X01 threat model as a **tampering/integrity** consideration on the analytics→automation boundary.

## Accessibility notes
Zones are DOM-mirror region markers with an `aria-label` describing the zone and state in words ("Buy imbalance stack, 4 levels, 63,980 to 64,010, unbroken"). Per the E18-D04 announcement policy, a **newly formed stacked zone is one of the three events that may be announced automatically** (the others are user focus movement and bar close) — at most one announcement per zone, politely. The tracker table supports keyboard row activation and the "only unfilled" filter is a labelled checkbox.

## Performance notes
Zone rendering must stay under 0.2 ms at the target scene; zone bookkeeping is off the render path. Marker updates coalesced to ≤ 10 Hz (US-FP-009 NFR applies to markers generally).

## Observability
Metrics: `footprint_stacks_rendered`, `footprint_zone_state_transitions_total{to}`, `stacked_imbalance_zone_events_total`. The event itself is observable on the bus for downstream epics.
