title: Mark bar POC, value area and unfinished auctions without flicker
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-009 — Bar POC and unfinished auction (Must/Should)**: intrabar point of control is Must, unfinished-auction markers are Should. *"I want the intrabar point of control and unfinished-auction markers, so that I can read bar structure."* NFR: **marker updates coalesced to ≤ 10 Hz** — the third scenario requires both markers to update as the forming bar evolves *without flicker*.

`18-traceability-matrix.md` notes US-FP-009 as one of the stories that initially resolved to zero screens; it is now mapped to SCR-030 (markers) and SCR-032 (the toggles: "[x] bold per-bar POC  [x] mark VA").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Bar POC**: the highest-volume price level in each bar marked distinctly (bold cell border plus a text label, never fill colour alone) and exposed as a metric (`bar_poc_price`) so Deep-Stats (E20) and rules read the same value.
- **Value area**: VAH/VAL boundaries marked per bar using the server-computed `va_high_ticks`/`va_low_ticks`, with the configured `value_area_pct` (default 70%) shown in the legend.
- **Unfinished auction**: bars whose extreme has two-sided volume at the last level marked with an explanatory tooltip; the opposite case (`finished_auction_high/low`) is available in the cell detail but not marked on the canvas by default.
- SCR-032 toggles for both markers.
- Flicker-free forming-bar updates: marker position changes coalesced to ≤ 10 Hz with the E18-D04 motion spec (POC moving between levels animates within the bar; markers never blink).
- Marker rendering via CMP-195 AnnotationMarker, the shared sparse-event primitive.

## Out of scope
Session/visible-range profiles and their POC/VA (E19), naked-POC tracking (E19), the value-area **algorithm** itself (E18-T02 implements both `single_step` and `two_row_tpo`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bar POC
  Then the highest-volume price level in each bar is marked distinctly
  And the POC price is exposed as a metric readable by Deep-Stats and rules

Scenario: Unfinished auction
  Given a bar's extreme has volume on both bid and ask at the last level
  Then it is marked as unfinished with an explanatory tooltip

Scenario: Live bar updates without flicker
  Given the forming bar's POC changes level several times per second
  Then marker updates are coalesced to at most 10 Hz
  And no marker appears and disappears more than once per 200 ms

Scenario: Single-level bar is never unfinished
  Given a bar with exactly one traded level
  Then neither unfinished_high nor unfinished_low is marked

Scenario: Value area reflects the configured percentage
  Given value_area_pct is changed from 70 to 80
  Then VAH and VAL boundaries recompute immediately from cached cells with no refetch
  And the legend shows the active percentage

Scenario: POC is deterministic on ties
  Given two levels with identical maximum volume
  Then the marked POC is stable across re-renders and matches the server tie-break order

Scenario: Not colour-only
  Given a greyscale render
  Then POC, VAH/VAL and unfinished-auction markers remain identifiable by border weight, pattern and text label
```

## Technical notes / design
- All four values (`poc_price`, `value_area_high`, `value_area_low`, `unfinished_auction{high,low}`) arrive on the `FootprintUpdate` payload and in `FootprintBar` from REST — the client never recomputes them, for the same agreement reason as imbalance flags.
- The POC marker is a border/label treatment on an existing cell instance plus one annotation marker; it adds no per-cell cost.
- The ≤ 10 Hz coalescing is implemented in the same update pipeline as the forming-cell coalescing from E18-T01/T04, not as a second timer.


**Estimate rationale (re-baselined 55-pt train fit):** 3 → 2. Both algorithms (POC tie-break, value area `single_step`/`two_row_tpo`) are delivered and unit-tested by E18-T02, and markers are drawn through the shared CMP-195 AnnotationMarker primitive; the remaining work is marker placement, the SCR-032 toggles and the ≤10 Hz coalescing that E18-D04's motion spec already specifies.

## Test plan
- Unit: marker placement from payload fields; coalescing timer; single-level-bar suppression; legend percentage rendering.
- Integration: a forming-bar replay at full tick rate asserting the marker update count per second is ≤ 10 and no blink occurs.
- Golden image: POC, VA boundaries and unfinished markers, per theme, plus greyscale.
- E2E: toggle both markers in SCR-032 and assert the canvas and the SCR-045 table agree.
- Parity: POC/VA/unfinished flags covered exactly (not within tolerance) by E18-T06.

## Security notes
No new surface.

## Accessibility notes
POC and value-area status are conveyed by border/pattern plus a text label, **never fill colour alone** (CMP-110's stated contract, applied here to cells). The DOM-mirror label for a POC cell includes "point of control"; VA boundary cells include "value area high/low"; an unfinished-auction bar's mirror includes the explanation text rather than only a marker. Tooltips are keyboard-reachable. Marker changes on the forming bar are **not** announced (E18-D04 policy) — announcement happens on bar close only.

## Performance notes
Markers are sparse; target < 0.1 ms added at the target scene. The 10 Hz coalescing exists specifically to keep marker churn out of the frame budget.

## Observability
Metric `footprint_unfinished_auction_total{end}`, `footprint_poc_moves_per_bar` (histogram, a proxy for flicker risk).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios pass via automated tests.
- [ ] Flicker assertion green against a full-rate forming-bar replay.
- [ ] Golden images and greyscale evidence committed.
- [ ] `bar_poc_price` metric exposed and verified readable by the metrics registry (the contract E20 depends on).
- [ ] axe-core green; mirror labels verified.

body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-010 — Footprint settings panel (Must)**: *"I want one panel for all footprint settings, so that I can tune quickly mid-session."* Screen **SCR-032**, described in `14-screens-catalogue.md` as *"the deepest settings surface of the chart"*. ## Scope / Deliverables

- **Live preview** (CMP-228 PreviewTile, `kind: "footprint"`): a synthetic bar rendering with the current settings, updating in ≤ 50 ms, with a textual description of what changed.
- **Per-symbol defaults**: "save as default for BTCUSDT" applies to new BTCUSDT footprint panes only; other symbols keep theirs.
- **Reset**: returns to product defaults (300% diagonal, stack 3, bucket 1 tick) behind a confirmation.
- Validation with inline errors: imbalance ratio 100–2000% ("Enter a ratio between 100 and 2000 %."), stack depth 2–10, noise filter ≥ 0, auto-hide threshold ≥ 0.
- Recompute-in-progress state ("Recomputing footprint from recorded trades — 40 %") for the one setting that triggers it (input source).
- **Cost warning**: when the selected combination was measured below budget, show the designed warning with the measured figure ("This tick aggregation renders ~180 cells per bar; measured 41 fps on your machine").
- RBAC: a `viewer` may change display-only settings for their own session but cannot trigger a recompute (`recording:write`); the control reflects that rather than failing on click.

## Out of scope
The rendering behaviours the settings drive (E18-S01..S09), the recompute job (E18-T05), the imbalance tracker panel (E18-S07/S08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live preview
  When I change a setting
  Then the chart updates immediately and the panel shows the effective value
  And the preview tile re-renders within 50 ms

Scenario: Per-symbol defaults
  When I save settings as the default for BTCUSDT
  Then new BTCUSDT footprint panes adopt them
  And other symbols keep their own settings

Scenario: Reset
  When I choose reset
  Then a confirmation is required
  And on confirm settings return to 300 percent diagonal, stack 3, bucket 1 tick

Scenario: Validation
  When I enter an imbalance ratio of 2500 percent
  Then an inline error reads "Enter a ratio between 100 and 2000 %."
  And the setting is not applied

Scenario: Only the input source rebuilds
  When I change any setting other than the input source
  Then no recompute job is started and the chart updates from cached aggregates
  And when I change the input source, the recompute progress state is shown

Scenario: Below-budget combination is guarded
  Given a tick aggregation measured below the frame budget on this machine
  Then the dialog shows the measured cost warning before the setting is applied

Scenario: Viewer cannot rebuild
  Given a user with the viewer role
  Then the input-source control is shown in a permission-denied state
  And attempting to change it neither issues a request nor silently fails
```

## Technical notes / design
- The dialog is a controlled form over `FootprintOptions`/`FootprintConfig`; there is exactly one settings object per pane, and "save as default for symbol" writes to user preferences rather than duplicating state.
- The preview tile drives a miniature engine instance with synthetic data — not a screenshot, so it is honest about the actual renderer.
- The cost warning reads from the locally measured benchmark result stored by the SET-005 "Run benchmark" action (`14-screens-catalogue.md` performance settings section) when present, and otherwise from the E18-K01 reference-machine figures with that provenance stated.

- Unit: form state; validation boundaries (99/100/2000/2001%, stack 1/2/10/11); per-symbol default resolution; reset confirmation; permission-gated control state.
- E2E: change each control and assert the chart reflects it; assert only the input-source change issues a network request; save a per-symbol default, open a new pane and assert adoption.
- Perf: preview re-render ≤ 50 ms measured.
- axe: full dialog, including the colour controls and their paired glyph/pattern options.

## Security notes
The recompute action is state-changing, `recording:write`-gated and audited (`chart.footprint_settings_changed`, `market.footprint_recompute_requested`). Client-side gating is a UX affordance only — the server enforces (E18-T03). Settings apply without a full history refetch except for input-source changes (SCR-032 performance note). Preview renders in ≤ 50 ms. The dialog must not hold a second full engine instance alive after it closes — assert no leak in the memory soak.

`chart.footprint_settings_changed` with `{section, key}`; `market.footprint_recompute_requested` audit; metric `footprint_settings_reset_total`.

title: Make footprint cells keyboard-navigable and screen-reader accessible
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion 10 requires *"a11y pass on every new view incl. keyboard-navigable footprint cells and DOM ladder"*, and the R2 a11y quality gate states *"Footprint cells and DOM rows reachable and announced via the DOM-mirror."* CMP-109's catalogue entry specifies the mechanism: **every cell is mirrored** by an off-screen DOM node per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.1's canvas control surrogate pattern.

E18-S01 ships the mirror nodes; this story ships the **navigation, announcement policy and parity** that make them usable, plus the SCR-045 footprint content.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Keyboard cell navigation on SCR-030: arrow keys move focus cell-to-cell along the price axis (↑/↓) and the time axis (←/→); `Enter` opens the cell-detail Drawer (CMP-046); `Esc` returns focus to the pane; `Home`/`End` jump to the first/last cell of the bar; `PageUp`/`PageDown` move by bar group. The crosshair follows the focused cell (SCR-030's "crosshair is fully keyboard-driven").
- `aria-label` composition per cell: "Price 65,430; bid 12.4; ask 8.1; delta +4.3", extended with "buy imbalance 420 percent", "part of a 4-level stack", "point of control", "value area high/low" and the unfinished-auction explanation where applicable. Full values **regardless of zoom-driven text hiding**.
- Implementation of the **E18-D04 announcement policy**: nothing is announced for forming-cell value changes; announcements occur only on explicit focus movement, on bar close, and on a newly formed stacked zone. A polite live region, never assertive.
- **SCR-045 parity** (`Alt+T`): the data-table alternative exposes the visible range with per-bar time, OHLC, volume, delta, CVD and an **expandable per-bar footprint cell list** (price, bid, ask, delta, imbalance flag) — the exact content the catalogue specifies — with `B`/`A` glyph carriers so sides are never colour- or position-only.
- Mirror recycling: nodes exist for **visible** cells only and are pooled, so the DOM never grows with loaded history.
- Canvas `role="img"` rolling summary maintained ("BTCUSDT 1 minute, last 64 011, up 0.4 %, delta +200").
- Focus ring drawn on the canvas for the focused cell, visible at every LOD level including text-hidden.

## Out of scope
The DOM ladder's own a11y (E21), the full SCR-045 screen for non-footprint content (E12/E20 contribute their columns), the a11y audit itself (E18-Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cell-to-cell navigation
  Given focus is on a footprint cell
  When I press the up arrow
  Then focus moves to the next price level in the same bar and the crosshair follows
  And when I press the right arrow, focus moves to the same price level in the next bar

Scenario: Full values below the text threshold
  Given the zoom level hides cell numerals
  When a cell receives focus
  Then its announced label still contains the full bid, ask and delta values

Scenario: Screen-reader chatter is bounded
  Given the forming bar updates 10 times per second
  Then no announcement is emitted for those updates
  And announcements occur only on focus movement, bar close and a newly formed stacked zone

Scenario: Table alternative parity
  When I press Alt+T
  Then SCR-045 lists the visible bars with time, OHLC, volume, delta and CVD
  And each bar expands to its footprint cells with price, bid, ask, delta and imbalance flag
  And the values match the canvas exactly for the same visible range

Scenario: The DOM does not grow with history
  Given 100000 bars are loaded
  Then the number of mirror nodes is proportional to visible cells only
  And a memory sample shows no monotonic growth as the user pans

Scenario: Focus is always visible
  Given any LOD level including text-hidden and profile display mode
  Then the focused cell has a visible focus indicator meeting contrast requirements

Scenario: Enter opens the detail drawer
  When I press Enter on a focused cell
  Then the cell-detail drawer opens with focus moved into it
  And Esc closes it and returns focus to the originating cell
```

## Technical notes / design
- The mirror is an `aria-hidden="false"`, visually-hidden container positioned off-screen, containing one focusable element per visible cell in DOM order matching reading order (bar by bar, price descending). Rebuild on viewport change is throttled to the LOD/viewport update, not per frame.
- Node pooling: reuse elements and update labels; creating and destroying hundreds of nodes per pan would itself break the frame budget.
- Focus synchronisation is bidirectional: canvas crosshair movement updates DOM focus and vice versa, through one controller, so the two cannot disagree (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 4.4: desyncing the DOM-mirror accessibility layer from what is rendered is *never acceptable*, even under degradation).
- Announcement policy is implemented as a single gate in front of the live region, so a future feature cannot accidentally add chatter without touching that gate.

## Test plan
- Unit: label composition for every cell state; navigation key handling including edges (first/last bar, first/last level); pooling behaviour; announcement gate (assert silence for forming updates).
- E2E (Playwright): full keyboard-only traversal of a bar's cells; `Alt+T` parity check comparing table values against the engine's data for the same visible range; focus-return after the drawer closes.
- axe-core: SCR-030 with the mirror layer specifically, and SCR-045.
- Manual: screen-reader pass (NVDA and VoiceOver) recorded as evidence, per `03-testing-strategy.md`'s manual-SR requirement.
- Memory: mirror-node count asserted in the 2-hour chart-engine soak.

## Security notes
The mirror duplicates on-screen market data into the DOM; it contains no secrets. Ensure the mirror is excluded from screenshot/export paths so it cannot double-render into shared images. No new network surface.

## Accessibility notes
This story **is** the accessibility implementation for E18 and is the gate R2 exit criterion 10 checks. WCAG 2.2 AA specifics: 2.1.1 keyboard (all cell information reachable), 2.4.3 focus order (DOM order matches visual reading order), 2.4.7 focus visible (at every LOD), 1.4.1 use of colour (labels carry meaning in text), 4.1.2 name/role/value (each cell is a labelled, focusable element), 4.1.3 status messages (the bounded live region). `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured for crosshair/focus transitions.

## Performance notes
Mirror maintenance must add ≤ 1.0 ms per viewport update and **zero** per-frame cost when the viewport is static. Assert both. The mirror must not force layout thrash — batch DOM writes and measure with the frame harness.

## Observability
Metrics: `footprint_mirror_nodes` (gauge), `footprint_mirror_rebuild_duration_seconds`, `a11y_announcements_total{surface="footprint"}` (used to prove the chatter bound in CI).

## Scope / Deliverables

- Pydantic models exactly as in section 4.1: `FootprintCell` (`price_ticks`, `price`, `bid_volume`, `ask_volume`, `total_volume`, `delta`, `trade_count`, `buy_count`, `sell_count`, `max_trade_qty`, `first_ts`, `last_ts`), `ImbalanceFlag`, `BarFootprint` (including `spec_hash`, `tick_size`, `price_origin`, `aggregation_ticks`, `poc_ticks`, `va_high_ticks`, `va_low_ticks`, `value_area_pct`, `unfinished_high/low`, `total_volume`, `delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta`).
- `FootprintConfig` per section 4.7 with every documented default.
- Side attribution: `if trade.side == "buy": ask_volume += qty else: bid_volume += qty` - Bybit reports the taker side directly, so no aggressor reconstruction.
- Grid keying on integer ticks: `price_ticks = round((price - price_origin) / tick_size)`; `price_origin` constant per symbol per `metadata_version`.
- **Sparse** cell storage - only traded levels materialise.
- Price aggregation applied **after** native accumulation: `bucket = floor_div(price_ticks, aggregation_ticks) * aggregation_ticks`; auto mode picks `max(1, ceil(bar_range_ticks / 60))` per viewport, cached per bar-range bucket.
- Per-bar rollups: `delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta`, `total_volume` maintained incrementally.
- Coalescing: forming-bar footprint emitted at most every 100 ms; the closing update always emitted immediately.
- Memory policy: evict `BarFootprint` beyond the 2 000 most recent bars per (symbol, spec); re-materialise from storage on scroll-back (the read path is E18-T05's).
- `metadata_version` bump invalidates cached aggregates for that symbol and schedules a rebuild (section 13.6).
- Aggregation window for US-FP-005: prints at the same price, side and millisecond merged before display, window configurable 0-100 ms; changing it re-aggregates from stored prints.

## Out of scope
Imbalance / POC / value-area / unfinished-auction algorithms (E18-T02); persistence and the cold tier (E18-T05); REST (E18-T03) and WS (E18-T04) surfaces; any rendering.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cells accumulate at native tick resolution
  Given a recorded stream of BTCUSDT trades across one 5m bar
  When the engine processes them
  Then each traded price level has one cell keyed by integer price_ticks
  And bid_volume holds taker-sell quantity, ask_volume holds taker-buy quantity, and delta equals ask_volume - bid_volume for every cell

Scenario: Aggregation is display-time and lossless
  Given cells accumulated at aggregation_ticks = 1
  When recompute_flags is called with aggregation_ticks = 5
  Then levels are bucketed by floor_div(price_ticks, 5) * 5
  And no trade is re-read from storage
  And re-calling with aggregation_ticks = 1 reproduces the original cells exactly

Scenario: Sparsity holds
  Given a bar spanning 400 ticks with 30 traded levels
  Then exactly 30 cells exist, not 400

Scenario: Forming-bar emission is bounded
  Given 500 trades arriving within one second on the forming bar
  Then at most 10 FootprintUpdate emissions occur for that bar in that second
  And the bar-close update is emitted immediately regardless of the coalescing window

Scenario: A tick-size change invalidates the grid
  Given instrument metadata_version increments with a new tick_size
  Then cached aggregates for that symbol are invalidated and a rebuild is scheduled
  And no cell keyed on the old grid is served afterwards

Scenario: Memory is bounded
  Given 10 000 bars processed for one (symbol, spec)
  Then at most 2 000 BarFootprint objects are resident
  And requesting an evicted bar triggers re-materialisation rather than returning empty
```

## Technical notes / design
- Numeric conventions (`24-internal-schemas.md` C3/C5): `float`/`numpy` is permitted **inside** the engine; any value crossing into OMS/journal/audit is converted at the boundary via `Decimal(str(x)).quantize(...)`. Prices are `Decimal` at the boundary and integer ticks inside the grid; the integer form is derived, never authoritative.
- Hot path: per-trade work must be O(1) - a dict keyed by `price_ticks` per forming bar, with incremental rollups. No per-trade re-scan of the cell set.
- Concurrency: one engine instance per (symbol, bar spec); symbol-sharded per `20-architecture.md`'s scaling note. Never rely on free-threaded CPython.
- Error codes: an out-of-grid price (price below `price_origin` producing a negative tick index) is a data-integrity event - log at error with symbol and metadata_version, drop the trade from the cell grid, increment `footprint_grid_reject_total`; do not crash the ingestion loop.
- Config keys: `orderflow.footprint.max_resident_bars` (default 2000), `orderflow.footprint.forming_emit_ms` (default 100), `orderflow.footprint.agg_window_ms` (default 0, range 0-100).

## Test plan
- Unit: side attribution both directions; integer keying including negative offsets and rounding at exact half-ticks; sparsity; bucketing round-trip; incremental rollups vs a batch recompute over the same trades; aggregation-window merging at 0 ms and 100 ms; eviction and re-materialisation; metadata_version invalidation; out-of-grid rejection. >= 85% line coverage.
- Property-based: for random trade streams, `sum(cell.total_volume) == bar.volume` and `bar.delta == sum(cell.delta)`.
- Integration: recorded fixtures - normal session, high-volatility burst, thin-book symbol.
- Perf: 50 000 trades/s sustained single-symbol ingestion with the engine attached, asserting the backend-internal budget #6 (<= 20 ms p95 ingestion -> fan-out) is not breached by footprint work.

## Security notes
Market data, non-secret. Threat: **resource exhaustion** - a symbol with a pathological tick size could produce an unbounded cell count per bar; the sparse model bounds it by traded levels, and `orderflow.footprint.max_resident_bars` bounds history. Input validation: trade quantities and prices are validated against the instrument's `tick_size`/`qty_step` before entering the grid. No user input reaches this engine directly (configuration arrives already validated from E18-T03).

## Accessibility notes
N/A (no UI surface).

## Performance notes
Per-trade cost must stay within the ingestion budget: budget #5 (throughput per symbol), #6 (<= 20 ms p95 backend-internal), #11 (<= 0.5 vCPU per symbol steady-state), #8 (<= 300 MB per symbol working set). Benchmark the per-trade path in isolation and record the ns/trade figure on the ticket.

## Observability
Metrics: `footprint_cells_per_bar` (histogram, labelled symbol), `footprint_engine_trade_latency_seconds`, `footprint_resident_bars` (gauge), `footprint_eviction_total`, `footprint_grid_reject_total`, `footprint_forming_emissions_total`. title: Implement imbalance, unfinished-auction, POC and value-area algorithms
body:
## Context
The analytical layer over the cell grid. These are the numbers a trader acts on, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` sections 4.2-4.5 specify them precisely - including the edge cases that are *"the classic footprint bug"*. A wrong imbalance flag is worse than no flag, so this task implements the spec verbatim and proves it against fixtures.

All five algorithms are **display-time**: they run in `recompute_flags` over cached native-tick cells, never re-reading trades. That is what makes the SCR-032 controls instant.

## Scope / Deliverables
**4.2 Diagonal imbalance** - `buy_imbalance(P) = ask_volume(P) / bid_volume(P - tick)`, `sell_imbalance(P) = bid_volume(P) / ask_volume(P + tick)`; flag when `>= ratio`. Parameters: `ratio` default 3.0 (range 1.5-10.0), `min_volume` default 0, `diagonal_offset_ticks` default 1 (range 1-5) with **effective offset = `diagonal_offset_ticks * aggregation_ticks`**, `zero_policy` default `treat_as_min`.
- **Zero-denominator rule**: `treat_as_min` substitutes `min_volume_floor = max(min_volume, smallest_qty_step)`; `skip` never flags; `infinite` always flags. When the user leaves `min_volume` at 0 it defaults to `qty_step`, which is what stops a single 1-contract print manufacturing a 300% imbalance.
- **Edge levels**: the lowest cell has no `P - tick` neighbour and the highest no `P + tick`; missing neighbours outside the bar's traded range count as zero volume and therefore obey `zero_policy`.

**4.3 Stacked imbalance** - group consecutive `price_ticks` (step == `aggregation_ticks`) with the same direction; runs of length `>= min_stack` (default 3) get `stacked=True` and a shared `stack_id`. `allow_gaps` default false (an untraded intermediate level breaks the run; when true a single missing level is bridged but the bridged level is not itself flagged). `min_stack_volume` default 0. **Two adjacent runs of opposite direction never merge.** Stacked imbalances are published as the `stacked_imbalance_zone` domain event consumable by alerts and rules.

**4.4 Unfinished auction** - `unfinished_high` when the bar's high tick equals the max traded cell and that cell has `bid_volume >= min_side_volume` **and** `ask_volume >= min_side_volume`; symmetrically for the low. `min_side_volume` defaults to `qty_step`. `min_extreme_pct` default 0.0. Edge cases: a bar with exactly one traded level is **never** unfinished at either end (return False for both); a one-sided extreme cell is a *finished* auction, exposed separately as `finished_auction_high/low`.

**4.5 Per-bar POC and value area** - `poc_ticks` = max `total_volume` cell with the deterministic tie-break ladder (a) closest to the bar's VWAP, (b) closest to bar `close`, (c) lower `price_ticks`. Value area: target = `total_volume * value_area_pct` (default 0.70); from the POC repeatedly compare the cell above the current VA high with the cell below the current VA low and absorb the larger; **ties absorb both**; when one side is exhausted continue on the other; stop at `>= target`. `value_area_algorithm` offers `single_step` (default) and `two_row_tpo`; **both are implemented and unit-tested against the same fixture**.

## Out of scope
Cell accumulation (E18-T01), transport (E18-T03/T04), rendering, the E25 detector inspector.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default diagonal imbalance
  Given ask volume at price P exceeds bid volume at P minus one tick by 300% or more
  Then a buy imbalance is flagged at P with the actual computed ratio recorded

Scenario: Zero denominator does not manufacture signals
  Given a level whose diagonal comparison cell has zero volume
  And zero_policy is treat_as_min with min_volume left at 0
  Then qty_step is substituted as the denominator floor
  And a single one-contract print does not produce a flag at the default ratio
  And with zero_policy = skip no flag is produced, and with infinite a flag always is

Scenario: Effective offset scales with aggregation
  Given aggregation_ticks = 5 and diagonal_offset_ticks = 1
  Then the comparison cell is 5 ticks away, not 1

Scenario: Stacked runs respect gaps and direction
  Given three consecutive same-direction flagged levels with allow_gaps false
  Then they form one stack with a shared stack_id
  And inserting an untraded level in the middle breaks the run into two sub-min_stack runs
  And with allow_gaps true the run survives with the bridged level itself unflagged
  And a buy run adjacent to a sell run never merges

Scenario: Unfinished auction edge cases
  Given a bar with exactly one traded level
  Then both unfinished_high and unfinished_low are False
  And given a bar whose extreme cell has volume on only one side
  Then that end is reported as finished_auction, not unfinished

Scenario: POC ties are deterministic
  Given two cells with identical maximum total_volume
  Then the POC is the one closer to the bar VWAP, else closer to close, else the lower price_ticks
  And re-running the computation yields the same POC every time

Scenario: Value area expansion
  Given value_area_pct 0.70 and a fixture with a known expected VA
  Then single_step reproduces the documented expected boundaries
  And a tie between the upper and lower candidate absorbs both
  And two_row_tpo reproduces the reference-platform boundaries for the same fixture

Scenario: Display-time recompute never touches trades
  When ratio, min_stack, value_area_pct, zero_policy or aggregation_ticks changes
  Then recompute_flags produces new flags from cached cells with zero storage reads
```

## Technical notes / design
- Implement each algorithm as a pure function over the cell tuple so it is directly unit-testable and reusable by the offline DuckDB recomputation in E18-T06.
- `ImbalanceFlag.ratio` carries the **actual computed ratio**, not the threshold, because SCR-056 displays it ("420%").
- Stack detection runs after flag computation over ascending `price_ticks`; `stack_id` is stable within a bar recompute so the UI can diff zones without flicker.
- The `stacked_imbalance_zone` domain event carries symbol, bar index, price range, direction, stack size, aggregate volume and the config that produced it - E25/E40 consume it, so the payload is a contract; add it to `24-internal-schemas.md` section 7 if not already present.
- Note the accepted approximation recorded in the spec (research 08 section 4, open Q #9): the textbook TPO algorithm expands two rows at a time; `single_step` is our default and `two_row_tpo` exists for parity.

## Test plan
- Unit: one test per numbered scenario above, plus a table-driven suite over `ratio` in {1.5, 3.0, 5.0, 10.0} x `zero_policy` in all three values x `aggregation_ticks` in {1, 5}. >= 85% coverage.
- Golden fixtures: hand-computed expected flags for a small synthetic bar, checked into `tests/golden/footprint/`.
- Cross-validation: both value-area algorithms against the same fixture, with the documented difference asserted rather than hidden.
- Property-based: flags are invariant to the order in which trades arrived (they depend only on final cell state); recompute is idempotent.
- Integration: high-volatility burst fixture - assert flag counts are stable across two runs (determinism, an R2 exit criterion).

## Security notes
All parameters arrive from user input via E18-T03/T04 and must already be range-validated there (`ratio` 1.5-20 at the API, `min_stack` 2-10, `value_area_pct` 50-95); this task additionally clamps defensively and rejects out-of-range config with a typed error rather than computing nonsense. Threat: **algorithmic DoS** - `allow_gaps` with a large aggregation could in principle scan long runs; the scan is linear in cell count, which is bounded by traded levels, so the bound is inherited from E18-T01.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (no UI), but the flag payload must carry everything the non-colour encodings need: direction, ratio, stacked, stack size. A renderer must never have to infer direction from a colour choice.

## Performance notes
`recompute_flags` over 200 bars x 40 cells must complete in <= 30 ms so SCR-032 control changes feel instant; benchmark and record. The per-bar-close path runs inside the ingestion budget (#6, <= 20 ms p95 backend-internal).

## Observability
Metrics: `footprint_imbalances_per_bar` (histogram), `footprint_stacks_per_bar`, `footprint_recompute_flags_duration_seconds`, `footprint_unfinished_auction_total{end}`. Event: `stacked_imbalance_zone` published on the bus.

title: Serve GET /market/footprint and POST /market/footprint/recompute
body:
## Context
REST is the bootstrap-history surface: `23-ws-protocol.md` section 1.2 states bulk history for bars, footprint, profiles and metrics comes from REST, and the WS carries only the live tail plus the attach snapshot. Both endpoints already exist in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; this task implements them against the engine. Interface-first: the schema is merged, so any deviation requires an OpenAPI change reviewed before implementation (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` section 10).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /api/v1/market/footprint` with parameters `symbol`, `bar_type` (required), `param` (required, maxLength 24), `from`, `to`, `limit`, `price_grouping` (1-1000, default 1), `imbalance_ratio` (1.5-20, default 3), `min_stack` (2-10, default 3), `min_imbalance_volume`, `value_area_pct` (50-95, default 70). RBAC `marketdata:read`, scope none.
- Response `FootprintResponse`: `symbol`, `bar_type`, `param`, `tick_size`, `price_grouping`, `bars[]` of `FootprintBar` (Bar fields plus `poc_price`, `value_area_high`, `value_area_low`, `unfinished_auction{high,low}`, `cells[]`, `imbalances[]`), and `meta` (`DataMeta`, including `recording_started_at`, `sources`, `next_cursor`, `has_more`, `count`, `generated_at`).
- **Window bound**: `bars x price_levels <= 200 000 cells`, else `400` with `validation_failed` / `footprint_window_too_large` (RFC 9457 problem body). The UI paginates by bar.
- **Partial history**: `meta.recording_started_at` is always populated so the client can render the explicit partial-history state (global AC #7); bars before native tick data begins carry null delta/footprint fields rather than fabricated zeros.
- `POST /api/v1/market/footprint/recompute`: body `{symbol, bar_type, param, from, to, price_grouping?}`, requires an idempotency key and RBAC `recording:write`; returns `202` with `job_id`; progress polled via `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`. Used after an input-source change or to repair a window flagged by gap detection (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 13.3).
- Read path: hot window from QuestDB `footprint_cells`, older windows from the Parquet/DuckDB cold tier, transparently merged with `meta.sources` naming which tiers answered.

## Out of scope
WS topic (E18-T04); the persistence tables and export job themselves (E18-T05); any client code.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bootstrap a footprint window
  Given recorded BTCUSDT data for 2026-12-02
  When GET /api/v1/market/footprint?symbol=BTCUSDT&bar_type=time&param=5&from=...&to=... is called with marketdata:read
  Then 200 is returned with one entry per bar, each carrying cells, imbalances, poc_price, value_area_high/low and unfinished_auction
  And the response validates against the FootprintResponse schema

Scenario: Oversized window is refused, not truncated
  Given a window whose bars x price_levels exceeds 200000 cells
  Then 400 is returned with code validation_failed and detail footprint_window_too_large
  And no partial result is streamed

Scenario: Display-time parameters are honoured without a rebuild
  Given the same window requested twice with imbalance_ratio 3 then 2
  Then the second response has more or equal imbalance flags
  And no recompute job is created

Scenario: Partial history is declared
  Given the recorder started mid-window
  Then meta.recording_started_at names the first available timestamp
  And bars before it are absent rather than zero-filled

Scenario: Recompute is authorised, idempotent and asynchronous
  Given a user with marketdata:read but not recording:write
  When POST /market/footprint/recompute is called
  Then 403 is returned, nothing changes, and an audit record is written
  And with recording:write and an idempotency key, 202 with a job_id is returned
```

title: Publish the footprint WS topic with binary body_kind 5 and cell coalescing
body:
## Context
The live tail. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.1 already defines the topic contract; this task implements the publisher inside the gateway E17 built. The binary path matters: JSON decode of dense cell payloads produces GC garbage on every frame, which the 100 ms cadence cannot afford (section 3.1 decision note).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Topic `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with options `price_grouping`, `imbalance_ratio`, `min_stack`, `min_imbalance_volume`, `history` (<= 200). Snapshot = last `history` bars of cells. Default throttle 250 ms.
- Structured payload `FootprintUpdate` per section 14.4: `symbol`, `bar_type`, `param`, `tick_size`, `price_grouping`, `bars[]` with `t_ms`, `close_t_ms`, `confirm`, `poc_price`, `value_area_high`, `value_area_low`, `delta`, `unfinished_auction{high,low}`, `cells[]` (`price`, `bid_volume`, `ask_volume`, ...), `imbalances[]`.
- **Binary `body_kind` 5** per section 3.4: per-bar group `u32 ts_offset_ms`, `u32 cell_count`, then `cell_count` x 33 bytes: `i64 price`, `u64 bid_volume`, `u64 ask_volume`, `u32 trades`, `u8 flags` (bit0 buy-imbalance, bit1 sell-imbalance, bit2 in-stack, bit3 POC). Advertised via the `binary_footprint` capability in the `welcome` frame.
- **Coalescing** per section 8.2: per (bar, price) cell, values **summed** for the same bar and **replaced** across bars. Coalesced frames set `coalesced: true` (structured) or header flag bit1 (binary) and carry `coalesced_count`.
- Sequencing: the topic carries its own sequence domain. `footprint` and `bars` for the same `(symbol, bar_type, param)` are **separate subscriptions**, guaranteed consistent (same builder) but not frame-synchronised - the client keys them by bar open time. Document this in the subscribe-ack path.
- Unconfirmed bars: the last bar may carry `confirm: false`; never treat it as closed.
- Backpressure: per (conn, topic-class) queue depth 32 for footprint (section on bus->gateway buffers); when full, conflate; footprint detail is shed **before** bars and book top-N and **after** heatmap columns and profile recompute, per the priority ladder. Order-related work is never shed.
- Gap/resync: on a detected gap the server emits `resync_required` and the client re-snapshots; footprint holes during a book DESYNC are marked (failure mode F2 in `20-architecture.md`).

## Out of scope
Client decoding and rendering (E18-S01); REST bootstrap (E18-T03); the generic envelope, auth and sequencing machinery (E17).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Subscribe and attach
  When a client subscribes to footprint.BTCUSDT.time.5 with history 50 and encoding binary
  Then a snapshot of the last 50 bars of cells is sent, followed by deltas on the same sequence domain
  And the subscribe ack echoes the resolved options

Scenario: Binary layout is exact
  Given a bar with 30 cells
  Then the binary body is 8 bytes of bar header plus 30 x 33 bytes
  And decoding it yields cell values identical to the structured payload for the same bar
  And flag bits 0..3 correspond to buy-imbalance, sell-imbalance, in-stack and POC respectively

Scenario: Coalescing sums within a bar and replaces across bars
  Given three forming-bar updates for the same bar within one throttle window
  Then the emitted frame carries the summed cell values, coalesced true and coalesced_count 3
  And a subsequent update for the next bar replaces rather than sums

Scenario: History option is bounded
  When a client requests history 500
  Then the subscription is rejected or clamped to 200 with the resolved value echoed in the ack
  And no unbounded snapshot is generated

Scenario: Unconfirmed bar is flagged
  Then the last bar of any frame carries confirm false until the bar closes
  And the closing update is emitted immediately rather than waiting for the throttle window

Scenario: Sequence gap triggers resync, not silent loss
  Given the footprint queue for a connection overflows
  Then a resync_required control frame is sent, the topic buffer is dropped, and the client re-snapshots
  And ws_resync_total increments
```

## Technical notes / design
- Prices and volumes in the binary layout are fixed-point integers scaled by the instrument's `tick_size`/`qty_step`; the scale is carried in the snapshot (`tick_size`, `price_grouping`) so the decoder never guesses.
- Per-subscription option resolution happens once at subscribe time; changing `imbalance_ratio` requires a re-subscribe or an option-update frame, and in both cases the server recomputes flags from cached cells (no storage read).
- Adaptive throttling (section 8.3) applies: under load the footprint throttle may widen; the client sees it through `coalesced_count`, which drives the "feed compressed" indicator rather than silently under-reporting activity.
- Error codes: unknown symbol/spec -> subscribe ack `ok:false` with a typed reason; option out of range -> clamp and echo, never silently ignore.

## Test plan
- Contract: WS JSON-Schema validation of `FootprintUpdate`; binary round-trip property test (encode -> decode -> equality) over random cell sets including empty bars and maximum cell counts.
- Unit: coalescing sum/replace semantics; history clamping; flag-bit packing; unconfirmed-bar handling.
- Integration: recorded fixtures with WS disconnect + resync and sequence gap; assert no duplicated or lost cells after resync.
- Load: k6 WS profile - 20 concurrent pane subscriptions across 10 symbols, asserting budget #3 (tick -> screen p95 < 100 ms) and budget #6 (backend-internal <= 20 ms p95), and bandwidth reduction >= 40% vs JSON per the ADR-0005 criterion.
- Chaos: kill the upstream Bybit WS mid-stream; assert the topic marks the hole and recovers.

## Security notes
Threats: **(D) DoS via unbounded subscription** - `history <= 200`, per-connection subscription caps and the bounded queue are the controls (this is the same class of vector the R2 gate calls out for E21); **(I) information disclosure** - the topic carries only public market data, but subscription patterns are behavioural data and must not be logged with user identifiers at info level; **(S) spoofing** - subscription requires an authenticated session established by E17. Rate-limit subscribe/unsubscribe churn to prevent snapshot-generation amplification (a client rapidly re-subscribing forces repeated 200-bar snapshots).

## Accessibility notes
N/A (transport), but `coalesced_count` must reach the client because the UI uses it for the honest "feed compressed" indicator rather than pretending the tape was quiet.

## Performance notes
Budgets #3 (tick -> screen p95 < 100 ms, hard R2 gate), #6 (<= 20 ms backend-internal p95), plus the ADR-0005 binary-encoding criteria (>= 40% bandwidth and >= 30% decode-time reduction vs JSON). Record all four figures on the ticket.

## Observability
Metrics: `ws_topic_frames_total{topic="footprint"}`, `ws_conflated_total{topic="footprint"}`, `ws_resync_total{topic="footprint"}`, `footprint_ws_bytes_total{encoding}`, `ws_subscription_count{topic="footprint"}`. Traces: publish span joined to the ingestion trace for budget #3 correlation.

title: Persist footprint_cells, export to the cold tier and implement the rebuild job
body:
## Context
Footprint history is what makes E19, E20, E23 and E26 possible, and R2's exit criterion 6 requires footprint values to match an independent offline recomputation over the Parquet tier for a full recorded symbol-day. The table already exists in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 4.9; this task wires the engine to it, exports to cold storage, and implements the rebuild that repairs gaps and metadata-version invalidations.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Writer for QuestDB `footprint_cells(ts, symbol, bar_family, bar_param, price, bid_volume, ask_volume, total_volume, delta, trade_count, buy_trade_count, sell_trade_count, max_trade_size, imbalance_flag, imbalance_ratio, is_poc, is_va, build_version)`, `TIMESTAMP(ts) PARTITION BY DAY WAL`, `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol, bar_family, bar_param, price)` - so a rebuild is an idempotent upsert, not a duplicate-producing insert.
- `build_version` increments on every rebuild so a reader can detect and prefer the newest build; readers filter to the max `build_version` per partition key.
- Cold export to `cold/footprint_cells/symbol=.../bar_family=.../bar_param=.../dt=.../part-NNNN.parquet` per section 5.1-5.2: Parquet v2, ZSTD level 6, 128 MiB row groups, rows sorted by `ts` then `price`, dictionary on `symbol`, `ts` as `TIMESTAMP(isAdjustedToUTC=true, MICROS)`, SHA-256 per file recorded in the manifest, exporter fails closed on column-set drift against `cold/_manifests/schema-registry.json`.
- DuckDB view `footprint_cells` over the cold parquet with hive partitioning (already declared in section 6 of the schema doc) - verify it resolves.
- Retention per section 8: hot 30 d, cold 12 mo, archive action `archive_parquet`, marked **rebuildable from `trades`**; pinning honoured.
- **Rebuild job** (the worker behind `POST /market/footprint/recompute`): replays recorded trades for a (symbol, spec, window) through `FootprintEngine`, upserts cells with an incremented `build_version`, reports progress to `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`, is resumable and cancellable, and is triggered by (a) an explicit user recompute, (b) a gap-detection repair, (c) a `metadata_version` bump invalidating the tick grid.
- Storage-growth accounting: the schema doc budgets ~1.2 M rows / 115 MB raw / ~20 MB compressed per symbol-day for `footprint_cells`; assert actual figures against that and report drift.

## Out of scope
The trade recorder itself (E16); the REST/WS surfaces (E18-T03/T04); analytics recomputation semantics (E18-T02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cells persist and read back identically
  Given one recorded symbol-day processed through the engine
  When cells are written and then read back for the same window
  Then every cell field round-trips exactly and cell counts match

Scenario: Rebuild is idempotent
  Given a window already persisted
  When the rebuild job runs twice for that window
  Then DEDUP UPSERT keys prevent duplicate rows
  And build_version increments each time
  And readers see exactly one cell per (ts, symbol, bar_family, bar_param, price)

Scenario: Cold export is verifiable
  When a day is exported to Parquet
  Then the manifest records a SHA-256 per file
  And the DuckDB view returns the same cell values as QuestDB did for that day
  And a deliberate column-set drift causes the exporter to fail closed rather than write a mismatched file

Scenario: Retention respects pins
  Given a pinned symbol-day older than the hot retention window
  Then it is not dropped from the hot tier
  And an unpinned day older than 30 days is archived to Parquet and removed from QuestDB

Scenario: A metadata_version bump schedules a rebuild
  Given the instrument tick_size changes
  Then cached and persisted cells keyed on the old grid are invalidated
  And a rebuild job is enqueued for the affected window
  And until it completes, reads for that symbol declare the affected range as rebuilding rather than serving mixed grids

Scenario: Rebuild is cancellable and resumable
  Given a rebuild covering 7 days is cancelled at 40%
  Then the job reports cancelled, completed partitions remain valid at their new build_version, and re-running resumes rather than restarting from zero
```

## Technical notes / design
- Writes batch per bar close, not per trade; WAL tables tolerate the batch cadence and the ingestion budget forbids per-trade synchronous writes.
- The rebuild reads trades from the hot tier when available and from Parquet otherwise, through the same repository interface so a TimescaleDB swap stays a swap and not a rewrite (ADR-0003).
- Concurrency: rebuild jobs bounded (`orderflow.footprint.recompute_max_concurrent`) and run at lower priority than live ingestion; a rebuild must never cause live footprint emission to miss budget #6.
- Config keys: `storage.footprint.hot_retention_days` (30), `storage.footprint.cold_retention_months` (12), `storage.footprint.export_row_group_mib` (128).

## Test plan
- Unit: writer field mapping; build_version increment; retention decision logic incl. pins.
- Integration: full symbol-day write -> export -> DuckDB read -> compare; deliberate schema drift; interrupted-export recovery; cancel/resume of a rebuild.
- Chaos: kill the process mid-export and assert no partial `part-NNNN.parquet` is registered in the manifest.
- Perf/soak: 24 h, 10 symbols ingestion soak asserting zero message loss and flat memory (R2 quality gate, budget #5); storage growth measured against the section 7 budget.

## Security notes
Threats: **(T) tampering / integrity** - SHA-256 per exported file in the manifest and in `backups.checksum_sha256`; **(D) DoS** - rebuild jobs are bounded in concurrency and are cancellable, so a user cannot exhaust IO; **(I) path handling** - partition values are constructed from validated symbol/bar-spec vocabularies and zero-padded date strings only; no user-supplied path component ever reaches the filesystem (the same class of issue the R2 gate flags for E26 archived-data path handling); **(R)** rebuild requests and retention actions are audited. Data classification: market data; the archive location inherits the host's disk encryption posture.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Budget #5 (ingestion, zero undetected loss), #12 (storage growth), #8 (memory per symbol). Persisted-write cost must not appear in the tick -> screen path: writes are off the hot path, and this is asserted by measuring budget #6 with persistence enabled and disabled.

## Observability

Logs: structured export start/finish with file checksums. Audit: `market.footprint_rebuild_started/completed`, retention actions.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] DuckDB view verified against QuestDB for a full symbol-day (this is the substrate E18-T06 depends on).
- [ ] Storage-growth measurement recorded against the `21-database-schema.md` section 7 budget.

title: Golden-fixture parity harness: served footprint vs offline DuckDB recomputation
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion 6 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 6.3) is explicit: *"Footprint, profile, CVD and Deep-Stats values match an independent offline recomputation (DuckDB over the Parquet tier) for a full recorded symbol-day, within floating-point tolerance."* The R2 quality-gate table adds: *"Golden-fixture tests: one recorded symbol-day with expected footprint/profile/CVD/Deep-Stats outputs version-controlled; any drift fails CI."* This task builds E18's half of that harness - and because E18 is first in the train, it establishes the pattern E19/E20/E23 reuse.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A version-controlled golden fixture: one full recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day (trades tape plus instrument metadata), stored per the fixture conventions of `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, with a documented provenance note (date, source, size, checksum).
- An **independent** recomputation implemented in SQL over the DuckDB Parquet views - deliberately *not* sharing code with `FootprintEngine`, because a shared implementation would agree with itself. It computes per-(bar, price) bid/ask volume, delta, trade counts, per-bar delta/min_delta/max_delta, POC, value-area boundaries, diagonal imbalance flags and stacked runs, and unfinished/finished auction flags, for a fixed `FootprintConfig`.
- A comparator asserting equality within documented tolerances: volumes and deltas within 1e-9 relative, ratios within 1e-6, and **exact** equality for all integer and boolean fields (cell counts, trade counts, POC tick, VA boundaries, imbalance direction, stacked flags, unfinished flags) - a POC that is "nearly right" is wrong.
- Expected-output artefacts committed so a drift is visible as a reviewable diff, not only as a red test.
- CI wiring as a **required check** on any change under the orderflow or chart-engine packages.
- A second fixture set for the edge conditions the R2 integration gate names: high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.
- A determinism assertion: recomputing the same window twice yields byte-identical output (feeds R2 exit criterion 7 and E26's replay determinism work).

## Out of scope
Profile, CVD and Deep-Stats parity (E19/E20/E23 extend the harness); replay double-run equality (E26); performance benchmarking (E18-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full symbol-day parity
  Given the golden fixture symbol-day and a fixed FootprintConfig
  When the served footprint window is compared with the DuckDB recomputation
  Then every cell, imbalance flag, stacked run, POC, value-area boundary and unfinished-auction flag matches within the documented tolerances

Scenario: Drift fails CI visibly
  Given a deliberate one-tick change to the POC tie-break order
  When CI runs
  Then the parity check fails and the diff names the affected bars and fields

Scenario: Edge fixtures are covered
  When the harness runs against the high-volatility, disconnect-resync, sequence-gap and thin-book fixtures
  Then parity holds, and for the gap fixture the harness asserts the gap is declared rather than silently interpolated

Scenario: Determinism
  When the same window is recomputed twice
  Then the outputs are byte-identical
```

## Technical notes / design
- The DuckDB implementation is the *specification executed a second way*: it is written directly from `24-internal-schemas.md` section 4 by a different engineer from the one who wrote `FootprintEngine`. State that reviewer requirement on the PR.
- Value-area expansion in SQL is awkward; implement it as a recursive CTE or a small deterministic Python-over-DuckDB routine that does not import engine code. Document which, and why, in the harness README.
- Tolerance rationale is recorded: floats accumulate differently under different summation orders, which is exactly why volumes get a relative tolerance while structural fields do not.
- Fixture size must stay reviewable - store the day as ZSTD Parquet and keep it under the repo's large-file policy; if it exceeds it, use the fixture-store mechanism defined in `03-testing-strategy.md` rather than committing a large binary.


**Estimate rationale (re-baselined 55-pt train fit):** 5 → 3. The five edge fixtures (high-volatility burst, disconnect+resync, sequence gap, thin-book, normal session) are recorded once by E18-Q02 and consumed here rather than authored twice; this ticket owns only the independent DuckDB recomputation, the comparator and the CI gate. The mutation/seeded-fault check is unchanged — the harness's job is to catch drift, and that is not where points were removed.

## Test plan
This ticket **is** test infrastructure. Its own verification: mutation testing - introduce each of five deliberate faults (wrong side attribution, off-by-one diagonal offset, zero-policy ignored, POC tie-break reordered, VA target using 0.7 of cell count instead of volume) and assert the harness catches all five. A harness that passes a known-broken engine is worthless.

## Security notes
The fixture is recorded public market data - no PII, no credentials. Confirm no API keys or account identifiers leaked into the recorded capture before committing (automated secrets scan over the fixture as part of the PR).

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The parity run must complete within the CI budget; target <= 5 minutes for the full symbol-day. If it exceeds that, shard by bar range and run the shards in parallel rather than reducing coverage.

## Observability
CI job emits the comparison summary (bars compared, fields compared, max observed deviation per field class) as a build artefact so slow drift is visible before it breaks the tolerance.

title: STRIDE threat model for the footprint epic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and the planning brief require a STRIDE threat model **per epic**, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 requires it to be scheduled at epic DoR. E18 is not a money-movement epic, but it introduces three genuinely security-relevant surfaces: an unbounded-by-default read endpoint, a resource-intensive rebuild job, and a high-fan-out WS topic — the same class of vector the R2 security gate flags for E21 ("unbounded subscription depth as a DoS vector") and E26 ("resource exhaustion, path handling"). It also creates an **analytics→automation boundary**: `stacked_imbalance_zone` events are consumed by the rule engine, so their integrity matters more than a chart decoration's.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model covering the E18 data flows: Bybit `publicTrade` → ingestion → `FootprintEngine` → (QuestDB/Parquet) → REST `/market/footprint` and WS `footprint.*` → client engine → DOM mirror; plus the recompute job flow and the domain-event flow to rules/alerts.
- Per category, with concrete controls and their owning ticket:
  - **Spoofing**: unauthenticated WS subscription or REST read (controls: session auth from E09/E17, `marketdata:read` on the endpoint).
  - **Tampering**: a client-side substitute computation disagreeing with server flags; a rebuild writing a mixed-grid result after a tick-size change; cold-tier file modification (controls: server-authoritative flags, `build_version`, SHA-256 manifests, `metadata_version` invalidation).
  - **Repudiation**: who requested a rebuild and with what parameters (control: audit `market.footprint_recompute_requested` with actor, role, payload).
  - **Information disclosure**: subscription patterns and watched symbols as behavioural data; verbose error bodies leaking internal paths or query fragments (controls: log hygiene, RFC 9457 bodies without internals).
  - **Denial of service** — the dominant category here: oversized windows (200 000-cell cap), `history` > 200 on the topic, subscription churn forcing repeated 200-bar snapshot generation, recompute spam, pathological tick-size/aggregation combinations, client-side unbounded allocation from a malformed `cell_count`.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a `viewer` triggering a `recording:write` rebuild; RBAC enforced server-side with a 403 that changes nothing and writes an audit record (global AC #1).
- Abuse cases written as executable expectations for E18-X02.
- Data classification statement: market data (public, non-secret) plus low-sensitivity behavioural data; no PII, no credentials, no financial account data on any E18 surface.
- Risk-register updates for anything new.
- Required-control list handed to E18-T03, E18-T04 and E18-T05 **before** they implement, per the interface-first rule.

## Out of scope
Implementing the controls (the T tickets do), penetration testing (E43, pre-R4), the replay and DOM-ladder models (E26/E21 own theirs).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every category is addressed
  When the model is reviewed
  Then each STRIDE category has either at least one identified threat with a named control and owning ticket, or an explicit justified "not applicable"

Scenario: DoS vectors are quantified
  Then each denial-of-service threat states the concrete limit that bounds it and where that limit is enforced
  And no limit is described as "reasonable" without a number

Scenario: Controls land before implementation
  Given the model is complete
  Then E18-T03, E18-T04 and E18-T05 each carry the required-control list before their implementation PRs open

Scenario: The automation boundary is modelled
  Then the stacked_imbalance_zone event flow to the rule engine is explicitly analysed for integrity
  And the control that a client cannot inject such an event is stated
```

Use the project's STRIDE template from `04-security-program.md`, with a data-flow diagram in mermaid matching the C4 L3 view in `20-architecture.md`. Reference the existing rate-limit and backpressure machinery from E17 rather than proposing parallel mechanisms.

## Test plan
The model's abuse cases become E18-X02's test cases; each must be written so it can be executed, not merely contemplated.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis. Output requires a Security engineer sign-off and is a DoR input for the implementing tasks.

Several controls are limits (window cap, history cap, recompute concurrency) that directly shape performance behaviour; coordinate the numbers with E18-Q03 so the security limit and the performance budget agree rather than contradict.

## Observability
Model names the detective controls: `footprint_window_rejected_total`, `ws_resync_total{topic="footprint"}`, `footprint_rebuild_jobs_total{status}`, subscription-churn rate, and the audit events — so an attack is visible, not merely blocked.

title: Security review and abuse-case testing of the footprint read and rebuild paths
body:
## Context
Executes the E18-X01 model against the built software. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 makes a Security engineer review mandatory for anything touching these paths before Done, and R2's security gate requires the DoS-class vectors to be closed before the train exits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case execution** against staging, each with a recorded result:
  1. Request a window exceeding 200 000 cells → expect `400 validation_failed / footprint_window_too_large`, no partial stream, bounded server memory.
  2. Subscribe with `history` = 5 000 → expect rejection or clamp to 200 with the resolved value echoed; no unbounded snapshot.
  3. Subscribe/unsubscribe churn at high rate on `footprint.*` → expect rate limiting; assert snapshot-generation amplification is bounded and observable.
  4. Fire repeated `POST /market/footprint/recompute` for the same and different windows → expect idempotency-key deduplication and concurrency limits; assert ingestion budget #6 is not breached while rebuilds run.
  5. Call both endpoints as `viewer`, `manager` and `owner` → expect the documented RBAC outcome; assert a 403 changes nothing and writes an audit record (global AC #1).
  6. Replay a recompute request with a reused idempotency key and with a tampered body → expect the documented behaviour, not a silent second job.
  7. Inject a malformed binary frame claiming an oversized `cell_count` → expect the client to reject and log, never to allocate unbounded.
  8. Attempt path traversal via `symbol`/`bar_type`/`param` reaching the cold-tier partition path → expect rejection at the vocabulary-validation layer, with no filesystem access attempted.
  9. Attempt to publish a forged `stacked_imbalance_zone` from a client connection → expect rejection; the event is server-produced only.
- **Automated rule coverage**: Semgrep/Bandit rules (or equivalents) for the recurring patterns this epic introduces — unvalidated window parameters reaching a storage query, user-influenced path components, and unbounded response materialisation — added to the SAST config so a future change cannot silently regress.
- **DAST**: OWASP ZAP pass over the new endpoints in the staging scan profile.
- **SCA/secrets**: confirm the new dependencies (if any) are clean; confirm the E18-T06 golden fixture contains no credentials or account identifiers.
- **Log hygiene review**: confirm no full query strings with user identifiers at info level, no internal paths in error bodies, and that audit records redact nothing that matters while exposing nothing that should not be.
- Findings triaged: fixed, or accepted-risk with an Owner-signed disposition.

## Out of scope
The threat model itself (E18-X01), penetration testing (E43), rendering-layer functional bugs (QA tickets).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is executed and recorded
  When the review completes
  Then each of the nine abuse cases has a recorded expected result, actual result and verdict

Scenario: DoS limits hold under pressure
  Given the oversized-window, history-overrun, churn and recompute-spam cases run concurrently
  Then the service stays within its CPU and memory budgets
  And no request path returns a partial or unbounded response
  And the detective metrics from the threat model increment as designed

Scenario: RBAC cannot be bypassed
  Given a viewer session
  Then neither endpoint performs a privileged action
  And every denial writes an audit record naming actor, role and attempted action

Scenario: Regressions are prevented, not just fixed
  Then SAST rules covering the identified patterns are merged into CI
  And a deliberately reintroduced unvalidated-window pattern is caught by those rules

Scenario: Findings are dispositioned
  Then every finding is fixed and re-verified, or recorded as accepted risk with Owner sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Execute against staging with fixtures, never live. Use the existing security-test harness conventions from `04-security-program.md`. Where a control lives in E17's shared machinery (rate limiting, backpressure), verify it applies to the `footprint.*` topic specifically rather than assuming inheritance — assumed inheritance is how gaps happen.

## Test plan
Each abuse case is written as a repeatable script where possible and added to the security regression suite, so R3/R4/R5 re-run them. Cases that must stay manual are marked with the reason.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security review required by DoD. It must be performed by the Security engineer, not by the implementing developer, and its sign-off comment is a hard gate on E18 reaching Done.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Cases 3 and 4 are explicitly run while measuring budgets #6 and #11, since a "limit" that protects availability by destroying latency is not a working control.

## Observability
Verifies the detective controls actually fire: `footprint_window_rejected_total`, `ws_resync_total{topic="footprint"}`, rate-limit counters, `footprint_rebuild_jobs_total{status}` and the audit stream. An unobservable control is treated as a finding.

- [ ] ZAP pass completed; findings triaged.
- [ ] SCA and secrets scans clean, including the golden fixture.
